records.description: The ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship is an SMU-administered award for applicants who are citizens of ASEAN member countries other than Singapore, applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at Singapore Management University. SMU publishes 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant, plus an annual living allowance of S$5,800, an annual accommodation allowance of S$3,000 and a one-time computer allowance of S$1,750 on enrolment. The scholarship itself carries no bond, but because the tuition coverage is conditional on accepting the MOE Tuition Grant, every international recipient is placed under the Ministry of Education's 3-year bond to work for a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation. Recipients must maintain a cumulative GPA of 3.0 out of 4.0, reviewed at the end of each academic term, and are liable to repay liquidated damages on breach.
records.best_fit: Applicants who are citizens of Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Thailand, Timor-Leste or Vietnam, who hold outstanding high school results, show strong leadership and co-curricular records, and are applying for a full-time undergraduate degree programme at SMU.
records.eligibility_summary: Eligibility criteria published by SMU: citizens from ASEAN member countries (excluding Singapore citizens); have strong leadership qualities and potential; present good co-curricular activities records; possess outstanding high school results; be applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at SMU. SMU lists the ASEAN member countries as Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste and Vietnam. Recipients must maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 out of 4.0, reviewed at the end of each academic term, and may not concurrently hold any other scholarship, bursary or university loan without prior written approval from the University. Applicants with international qualifications must also satisfy SMU's general admission requirement of at least 12 years of formal education and submit one standardised test score.

records.notes: SCOPE: the ASSIGNMENTS.md b132 row is 'SMU Undergraduate Scholarships for International Students', host smu.edu.sg, Singapore - the umbrella page https://admissions.smu.edu.sg/scholarships/prospective-students/international-students. That page lists three SMU-administered awards for international students (Lee Kong Chian Scholars' Programme, ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship, Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship) plus donor-funded awards. This record documents the ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship because it is the SMU-administered international award on that page for which SMU publishes complete current figures (full subsidised tuition coverage after the MOE Tuition Grant, S$5,800 annual living allowance, S$3,000 annual accommodation allowance, S$1,750 one-time computer allowance), an explicit renewal CGPA, explicit bond wording and a complete terms-and-conditions section. The other two were seen only as index-page listings. DUPLICATION: EXISTING_AWARDS.json already contains 'SMU Merit Scholarship' (Singapore Citizens only, bond-free, full four-year tuition waiver plus S$12,000 growth opportunities allowance) and 'SMU Global Impact Scholarship Award', both on admissions.smu.edu.sg; neither is this award, and a scan of all existing award names found no ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship entry, so this is not a duplicate. Slot b130 is the NTU ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship on ntu.edu.sg, a different awarding body and a different award, so it does not collide. FUNDING: funding_amount is the S$5,800 annual living allowance, the only single recurring figure SMU publishes; the tuition element is a coverage statement, not an amount. BOND: the scholarship itself carries no bond, but the mandatory MOE Tuition Grant means every international recipient serves a 3-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation, which forces fully_funded false. 75 PER CENT RULE: the widely stated Singapore scholarship condition that at least 75% of graduation credits be earned in Singapore was searched for and appears in NUS and NTU ASEAN scholarship terms, but is NOT published on SMU's ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship page; SMU instead publishes that overseas programmes of up to one academic term are allowed and not permitted in the final year. No 75% claim is asserted for SMU. LOGO: the dark header SVG was probed and confirmed to return real image bytes, contradicting the earlier audit note that this asset returned text/html. official_details.deadline_note: There is no separate scholarship deadline. Interview notifications for shortlisted applicants run January to July 2026, shortlisted applicants attend an interview or test between March and May, and outcomes are notified February to July 2026 in batches, consistent with the Singapore admissions timeline rather than a fixed scholarship deadline.

The published AY2026-27 admission cycle closed on 19 March 2026 and classes started on 17 August 2026, so at the verification date of 2026-10-03 the next cycle is expected but its dates are not yet published. official_details.funding_duration: Tenable for the duration of the full-time undergraduate degree programme at SMU, normally four years; the page publishes no separate maximum award period but states the scholarship covers Double Degree Programmes provided both degrees are completed within the standard four-year student tenure
official_details.tuition_coverage_note: The published benefit is '100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees (after MOE Tuition Grant - scholarship recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant)'. Two limitations keep fully_funded false. First, the coverage is of subsidised tuition fees only and is calculated after the MOE Tuition Grant, so any non-subsidised component and any compulsory ancillary, laboratory or miscellaneous fee is not stated to be covered. Second, and decisively, the coverage is conditional on accepting the MOE Tuition Grant, which for international students carries a 3-year bond to work for a Singapore-registered company immediately upon graduation; MOE confirms independently that 'Tuition Grant recipients who are Singapore Permanent Residents or international students must serve a 3-year bond after graduation.' An unavoidable service obligation means the record cannot be represented as fully funded.

award_holder_conditions: Must accept the Ministry of Education (MOE) Tuition Grant: 'While the ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship carries no bond, recipients are required to accept the Ministry of Education (MOE) Tuition Grant.'

MOE Tuition Grant bond: 'Singapore Permanent Residents and international students who accept the Tuition Grant will be subject to a bond requiring them to work for a Singapore-registered company for a period of three (3) years immediately upon graduation.'

MOE confirms the bond independently: 'Tuition Grant recipients who are Singapore Permanent Residents or international students must serve a 3-year bond after graduation.' Only full-time employment after graduation counts towards the bond, and MOE describes the employer as a Singapore entity, which may be a company incorporated in Singapore or a foreign company with a substantial connection to Singapore.
Academic performance: 'Scholarship recipients must maintain a minimum Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 3.0 out of 4.0. Academic performance will be reviewed at the end of each academic term.'

Overseas programme participation: 'Recipients may participate in overseas programmes lasting up to one academic term. Participation in such programmes is not permitted during the final year of study.'
Double Degree Programme coverage: 'The scholarship covers students enrolled in Double Degree Programmes, provided that both degrees are completed within the standard four-year student tenure.'
Withdrawal: 'The University reserves the right to withdraw the scholarship at any time if the recipient's academic progress or conduct is deemed unsatisfactory.'
Concurrent awards: 'Scholarship recipients may not concurrently hold any other scholarships, bursaries, or university loans without prior written approval from the University.'

Post-graduation employment: 'Scholarship recipients are responsible for securing their own employment to fulfill the obligations of the MOE Tuition Grant bond. SMU does not guarantee or provide job placement upon graduation.'
Termination and repayment: 'In the event of premature termination of the scholarship or breach of any of the stated terms and conditions, the recipient shall be liable to repay liquidated damages.'
supplements_or_initiatives: Overseas programmes of up to one academic term, permitted except during the final year of study

official_details.description: The ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship is an SMU-administered undergraduate award from Singapore Management University for applicants who are citizens of ASEAN member countries other than Singapore and who are applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at SMU. SMU publishes 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant, an annual living allowance of S$5,800, an annual accommodation allowance of S$3,000 and a one-time computer allowance of S$1,750 on enrolment. The scholarship carries no bond of its own, but because the tuition coverage is conditional on accepting the MOE Tuition Grant, every international recipient is placed under the Ministry of Education's 3-year bond to work for a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation. Recipients must keep a cumulative GPA of 3.0 out of 4.0 at the end of every academic term, may take at most one term of overseas programme outside the final year, and must repay liquidated damages if they breach the terms.
official_details.coverage: Subsidised undergraduate tuition fees in full after the MOE Tuition Grant, plus an annual living allowance of S$5,800, an annual accommodation allowance of S$3,000 and a one-time computer allowance of S$1,750. Overseas programmes are permitted for up to one academic term and excluded from the final year of study, but no airfare or travel funding is published.

alerts.trigger: Evaluating this award as full funding
alerts.message: SMU publishes 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees but only after the MOE Tuition Grant, and that grant carries a 3-year bond to work for a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation, with only full-time employment counting. Price the bond into any comparison rather than reading this as cost-free study.

SMU publishes no separate scholarship closing date. The award follows the undergraduate admission timeline, whose published closing date for international and other qualifications was 19 March 2026, 11.59pm, Singapore Standard Time for the AY2026-27 intake. Next-cycle dates were not published when this record was verified on 2026-10-03, so treat the deadline as variable rather than fixed.

The published cycle ran from mid-November to mid-March, shortlisted applicants attend an interview or test between March and May, and outcomes are released in batches from May to July. An application submitted after the closing date cannot be considered for the scholarship.

alerts.trigger: Test score deadline trails the application deadline
alerts.message: For AY2026-27 the application closed on 19 March 2026 but the standardised test score was due by 31 March 2026. Missing the second date after applying is an easy, avoidable loss.

alerts.trigger: Checking for a 75 per cent credits rule
alerts.message: The condition that at least 75% of graduation credits be earned in Singapore appears in the ASEAN scholarship terms of other Singapore universities, but SMU's own page does not state it. SMU publishes only that overseas programmes of up to one term are allowed and not in the final year. Confirm the credits position with SMU before assuming either rule.
The scholarship still applies to Double Degree Programmes only if both degrees are completed within the standard four-year student tenure.

submission_workflow: 1. Confirm ASEAN citizenship other than Singapore citizenship and check your qualification against SMU's list of accepted international qualifications.
2. Sit one accepted standardised test if you do not already hold one, and register for the electronic score send.
3. Complete the SMU online application for admission for a full-time undergraduate degree programme.

4. In the Scholarship section of that application, indicate interest in the ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship. There is no separate scholarship form, so an application that omits this is not considered.
5. Upload standardised test scores via Applicant's Self Service and submit the application before the published closing date, with the test score by its own later deadline.
6. Submit through the Applicant's Self Service Portal as the scholarship page requires.
7. If shortlisted, attend the interview or, for Law, the writing test.
8. If offered the scholarship and admission, accept the MOE Tuition Grant as part of the offer, since the tuition coverage depends on it.
9. On enrolment, keep the CGPA at or above 3.0 out of 4.0 in every academic term, avoid taking an overseas programme in the final year, and do not accept a concurrent award without written approval.

records.application_period: There is no single global application window. Each French embassy or consulate abroad sets its own selection calendar for the scholarships it awards, generally for the following academic year.
records.application_method: Not automatic on admission. The scholarship is applied for directly to the French embassy or consulate (Service de coopération et d'action culturelle) in the candidate's country of residence; separately, admission to a French institution is applied for through the national admissions platform for the degree level (the 'Etudes en France' platform, pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr, for first-year Licence applications).
records.description: The Bourse du Gouvernement Français is the umbrella status for French government scholarships awarded by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs for study, internship and short research or language stays in France. Most of them are awarded by the cultural cooperation services of French embassies and consulates abroad rather than in Paris. Campus France implements the awarded scholarship and publishes the official rate grid: EUR 900 per month for a Licence (bachelor's) or Master's level scholarship and EUR 1,850 per month for a doctoral one. Holders are exempted from the CVEC student contribution and from enrolment fees for national and engineering degrees in public higher education establishments under the Minister for Higher Education, but training fees and other living costs remain with the holder.
records.best_fit: Foreign students from a country served by a French embassy or consulate that runs a French Government Scholarship call at Licence level, who have been admitted or are applying to a French higher education programme and who accept the reporting and attendance obligations attached to scholarship-holder status.
records.eligibility_summary: The award targets foreign students. It is not open to French nationals. Nationality rules, subject areas, eligible levels and selection criteria are set by the awarding embassy or consulate for each country, so eligibility is defined per country; the ministry reserves some specific programmes for particular nationality groups. Applicants must be admitted to or applying to a French higher education programme and must sign and honour the scholarship-holder obligations.

records.notes: This record covers the Licence (bachelor's) level track of the Bourse du Gouvernement Français. It is deliberately NOT the France Excellence Eiffel scholarship, which is already in the database as a separate master's/doctoral record; Eiffel applications come from French institutions and do not cover Licence. Licence-level French Government Scholarships are awarded by French embassies and consulates, not by the ministry in Paris through a single central call. 'Bourse du Gouvernement Français' is an umbrella status covering several categories (bourses d'études, bourses de stage, bourses de séjour scientifique de haut niveau); this record covers the bourse d'études at Licence level.

official_details.application_cycle: Annual cycle; each French embassy or consulate abroad publishes its own call and deadline for the academic year it is awarding. No single central application window exists.
official_details.deadline_central_display: No central deadline. The ministry states: "Quel que soit leur pays de résidence, les candidats doivent donc, avant leur départ et suffisamment à l'avance, s'adresser directement à ces services situés dans leurs pays d'origine afin d'obtenir toutes les informations sur ces bourses : conditions d'attribution, calendrier de sélection, dossiers à constituer." Deadlines therefore close per country, set by the awarding embassy or consulate.
official_details.deadline_note: There is deliberately no central deadline. The Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs states that the majority of these scholarships are awarded by the cultural cooperation services of French embassies and consulates abroad, and that candidates must contact those services in their country of origin to obtain the attribution conditions, the selection calendar and the documents to assemble. The deadline_precision is therefore 'varies'. The only exact dates published centrally are admission dates for a Licence programme, which are a separate procedure and not the scholarship deadline.
official_details.status_note: The scheme is a standing annual programme rather than a single call with one deadline. Embassy and consulate calls open and close on their own national calendars, so the award is neither simply open nor simply closed on any single date. Verified against the ministry page last updated 5 August 2026.
official_details.funding_duration: Awarded for a fixed period tied to the programme, the course and the institution; the rate applies for the duration of the scholarship.
official_details.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition is covered only in part and only by exemption, not by payment. Campus France states that a French government scholarship holder, on presenting its scholarship or financial-support certificate, 'will be exempted from' paying the CVEC and from 'the payment of enrolment fees relating to pursuing a national degree or an engineering degree in public scientific, cultural, and professional establishments under the authority of the Minister for Higher Education' (Article R719-49 of the Education Code). Two limits are stated on the same page: the exemption does not extend to training fees ('Campus France does not cover the education fees and you are responsible for them') and Campus France does not reimburse enrolment or tuition fees already paid to the institution. fully_funded is therefore false: there are uncovered components (training fees, housing rent, most day-to-day living costs) and binding scholarship-holder obligations.

official_details.description: The Bourse du Gouvernement Français is the umbrella status for French government scholarships awarded by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs for study, internship and language stays in France. The majority are awarded by the cultural cooperation services of French embassies and consulates abroad rather than in Paris, so the Licence track is applied for and decided country by country. Campus France implements the awarded scholarship and publishes the official rate grid: EUR 900 per month for a Licence or Master's level scholarship and EUR 1,850 per month for a doctoral one. Holders are exempted from the CVEC and from enrolment fees for national and engineering degrees in public establishments under the Minister for Higher Education, but training fees and most living costs stay with the holder, and the status carries binding attendance, examination and reporting obligations.
official_details.coverage: Covers a monthly maintenance allowance of EUR 900 at Licence level (EUR 1,850 at doctoral level), exemption from the CVEC and from public-sector national-degree enrolment fees, social security affiliation with up to two months of interim cover, and air travel only where the ministry or the awarding embassy funds it. It does not cover training fees, housing rent or most day-to-day living costs.

alerts.message: There is no single global deadline. Each French embassy or consulate sets and closes its own selection calendar, so track the mission for your country rather than a central date.

Campus France publishes 'Bachelor's and Master's degree rate EUR 900' and 'Doctorate rate EUR 1,850' as the official government rate grid, so the Licence (bachelor's) level is a funded track, not master's-only.
Campus France states plainly: 'Campus France does not cover the education fees and you are responsible for them.' Confirm your programme's fee type before accepting.
The allowance stops if you do not send your enrolment certificate, social security certificate, examination results or address, or if you are unjustifiably absent from your place of study.
If your international travel was financed, you must return home when the scholarship ends unless you formally waive the return ticket.

submission_workflow: Identify the French embassy or consulate covering your country of residence and check whether it awards Licence-level French Government Scholarships
Request that mission's conditions, selection calendar and document list
Apply for admission to the French Licence programme on the 'Etudes en France' platform (first-year Licence: 1 October to 15 December for the entry year)
Submit the scholarship file to the mission by its own national deadline
After award, complete and sign the scholarship application form required by Campus France
On arrival, contact Campus France using the dedicated contact in your Pass Campus France and email proof of arrival to trigger the first allowance
Within three months, send your attestation d'affiliation to the French social security system
Through the year, respond to Campus France's enrolment certificate, first-semester evaluation and June examination-results requests

records.description: The Bowdoin Scholarship is Bowdoin College's institutional need-based grant. Bowdoin is need-blind for all students including international students and meets the full calculated need of every admitted student. Scholarships are grants that do not have to be repaid, and the aid package carries no loans. Qualifying for no-loan student aid is available to everyone, including students who reside outside the United States.

records.description: The Dean's International Award Program is Queen's University's automatic admission-award programme for international students entering the first year of a first-entry undergraduate degree programme in the Faculty of Arts and Science, the Smith School of Business (Bachelor of Commerce), the Stephen J. R. Smith School of Engineering and Applied Science, or the Faculty of Health Sciences (Bachelor of Health Sciences). It comprises four faculty awards - Arts and Science, Commerce, Engineering and Health Sciences International Admission Awards - published at CAD 5,000, 10,000, 15,000, 20,000 or 25,000 per year depending on faculty and standing, with a four-year duration renewable for three subsequent years. Each award requires no separate application, is made on academic achievement, and is available only to students paying international tuition fees.
records.best_fit: First-year international applicants to Queen's University in Kingston with a very high admission average who are entering Arts and Science, Commerce, Engineering and Applied Science, or the Bachelor of Health Sciences and will be assessed at international tuition. Queen's International Student Hub markets these as 'Automatic scholarships and awards for international students with an average of 90%+'.

records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be international students - Canadian citizens, students holding dual-citizenship and permanent residents of Canada do not qualify - and must be entering the first year of post-secondary education for the first time. They must be entering the first year of a first-entry undergraduate degree programme in the Faculty of Arts and Science, the Smith School of Engineering and Applied Science, the Smith School of Business (Bachelor of Commerce) or the Faculty of Health Sciences (Bachelor of Health Sciences), must be paying international student fees (international students paying domestic fees are excluded), and must be selected on academic achievement. Students in the Bachelor of Nursing program are excluded from the Health Sciences International Admission Award. Students with prior post-secondary education are not eligible for Queen's admission awards.

records.selection_notes: The award is not applied for: Queen's states 'You will be considered automatically for this award, no application required.' The stated criterion for all four faculty awards is academic achievement. The published value tiers (CAD 5,000 to CAD 25,000) indicate that the amount awarded is set by the strength of the admission record, but Queen's does not publish a tier-to-average mapping, a weighting, or a competition ratio. Renewal for the three subsequent years requires the student to continue to be registered full-time in a programme of study within the original faculty of admission. Where a student is selected for a named donor grade-based award, Queen's states the original automatic award may be replaced by that named award of equal or higher value.
records.notes: Chosen from several distinct international undergraduate awards published by Queen's because the Dean's International Award Program is the best documented: official umbrella name, published per-faculty dollar tiers, published 4-year renewable duration, published eligibility and published renewal conditions. Distinct awards on the same host that are NOT recorded here and must not be duplicated as this record: the International Entrance Scholarship (formerly Queen's University International Entrance Scholarship, CAD 9,000 total, one year, all programmes, four available, no application required), the Principal's Global Scholars Undergraduate Award (for forcibly displaced students entering through the Global Scholars pathway, renewable up to three subsequent years on a 2.0 GPA, no amount published), the Principal's Scholarship (CAD 7,000, one year), the Mehran Bibi Sheikh Memorial Entrance Scholarship (CAD 1,500, one year, two available) and the Killam American Scholarship (CAD 9,000, one year, US citizens and permanent residents only). The award is tuition-side and partial: CAD 25,000 per year is roughly half of Queen's published 2026-2027 international total costs of CAD 47,324.31 (Arts and Science), CAD 57,366.58 (Computing), CAD 63,424.42 (Commerce Years 1-2), CAD 61,867.57 (Engineering and Applied Science) and CAD 38,283.46 (Health Sciences on-campus Year 1). No bond, service obligation or work requirement is published, and no number of awards is published.

official_details.tuition_coverage_note: PARTIAL, TUTION-SIDE AWARD. Queen's does not state on the award pages whether the Dean's International Award Program is formally restricted to tuition or may be disbursed from the student's fee account, so tuition coverage is not claimed as true; what is official is that eligibility requires the student to be paying international student fees, and the money reduces the tuition and fee bill. It is partial in every case: the published tiers are CAD 5,000 to CAD 25,000 per year against Queen's published 2026-2027 international undergraduate total costs of CAD 47,324.31 (Arts and Science, all degrees excluding Computing), CAD 57,366.58 (Computing), CAD 63,424.42 (Commerce Years 1-2), CAD 61,867.57 (Engineering and Applied Science) and CAD 38,283.46 (Health Sciences on-campus Year 1). At the top tier the award covers roughly half of an Arts and Science, Engineering or Commerce bill and about two thirds of Health Sciences; at the bottom tier about a tenth. The award also leaves the Student Association Levy (CAD 100-110), ancillary fees including health and dental (CAD 1,466.51-1,526.96) and the UHIP international health plan (CAD 948) uncovered.

official_details.description: The Dean's International Award Program is Queen's University Kingston's automatic admission-award programme for international students entering the first year of a first-entry undergraduate degree programme in the Faculty of Arts and Science, the Smith School of Business (Bachelor of Commerce), the Stephen J. R. Smith School of Engineering and Applied Science, or the Faculty of Health Sciences (Bachelor of Health Sciences). It comprises four faculty awards - Arts and Science, Commerce, Engineering and Health Sciences International Admission Awards - published at CAD 5,000, 10,000, 15,000, 20,000 or 25,000 per year, with a four-year duration renewable for three subsequent years while the student stays registered full-time in a programme within the original faculty of admission. records.name: General Entrance Award program (GEA)
records.funding_type: Entrance scholarship and bursary (mixed merit, leadership, involvement and financial need)
records.duration: Awards may be one-time, or renewable for up to 4 years. Dalhousie states the yearly value range of entrance awards is "$1K to $80K" and that awards can run "over 4 years"; named international awards on the page are expressed as e.g. "$22,000 renewable for 4 years".
records.deadline: February 15. Dalhousie states: "The 2027-2028 General Entrance Award program opens on October 1, 2026, with an application deadline of February 15, 2027." The Info for International Students page repeats this for international undergraduates: "GEA is applicable to students coming direct from high school if you apply by February 15."
records.application_period: The 2027-2028 GEA cycle opened on October 1, 2026 and closes at its application deadline of February 15, 2027. Dalhousie reviews applications after the February 15 deadline and notifies successful applicants in the spring. A separate early-entrance route exists with an earlier acceptance date: early entrance award offers must be accepted by paying the admission deposit by January 31.
records.application_method: One application for the whole programme. The applicant completes the General Entrance Award application through the Dalhousie application portal at https://apply.dal.ca/apply/ after submitting (or alongside) the undergraduate admission application. If not yet accepted, the applicant must also apply to an undergraduate programme, complete the GEA application, pay the $70 CAD admissions application fee, and submit an official first-semester transcript or provincial student ID number. Financial or disability-related supporting documents are uploaded directly into the GEA application in the portal. Award decisions are based on Grade 12 first-semester final grades, which the school or issuing institution must send directly to admissions.documents@dal.ca to be considered official.
records.description: Dalhousie University publishes a single undergraduate entrance award programme, the General Entrance Award program (GEA), through which international students are considered for entrance scholarships, bursaries and hybrid merit/need awards. Dalhousie offers "more than 2,000 entrance awards (scholarships) each year" with an approximate yearly value range of "$1K to $80K", awardable one-time or renewable for up to four years. One GEA application puts a student forward for hundreds of awards, assessed on academic achievement, leadership and initiative, extracurricular involvement, community service, financial need and cultural identity, with each student assessed individually on the full application. Eligibility is explicitly open to international students: "All students—domestic and international—are eligible to apply." Applicants must be entering directly from high school (or be a mature student with no transferable post-secondary study), be starting in the Fall term, and meet the academic requirement, typically an 80% average or 26 predicted/anticipated IB points. Named international awards listed on the page include the CorpFinance International Limited (Kevin Andrews) Indian Scholarship ($15,000, Bachelor of Commerce, students from India), the Murray Family Jamaican Engineering Scholarship ($88,000, $22,000 renewable for 4 years, Bachelor of Engineering with preference for Civil Engineering, students from Jamaica, academic standing and financial need) and the international strand of the Sankofa Scholarships ($48,000, $12,000 per year renewable for 4 years, international student of Black/African descent from the Caribbean entering an undergraduate degree program). Awards are not a tuition waiver: they are applied to the student account in two equal instalments in mid-August and mid-December, and any residual after tuition and fees may be refunded.
records.best_fit: International students applying to Dalhousie directly from high school, or mature students with no transferable post-secondary study, who are starting in the Fall term and can supply Grade 12 first-semester final grades by the February 15 deadline. Also suitable for students whose admission route requires them to pay the $70 CAD application fee as part of the award application. Not suitable for transfer students with post-secondary study already completed, and not suitable for Winter or Summer entry, for which Dalhousie directs students to current student awards and bursaries instead.
records.funding_period: One-time, or renewable for up to 4 years.
records.eligibility_summary: Open to all students, domestic and international. The applicant must be applying directly from high school or be a mature student with no transferable post-secondary study, must be starting in the Fall term, and must meet the academic requirement, typically an 80% average or 26 predicted/anticipated IB points, calculated using the five courses required for the programme applied for. Award decisions rest on Grade 12 first-semester final grades; later grades are not used to reassess. Applicants need not be eligible for financial aid or student loans, because many awards rest on merit or involvement. Gap year students may apply provided they have not completed transferable post-secondary study. Transfer students are generally not eligible, with an exception for Indigenous Black and First Nations students from the Maritimes seeking the FNIB Scholarship. Award-specific restrictions apply on top of the general rules: several named awards are limited by nationality (India, Jamaica, Caribbean heritage) or by programme (Bachelor of Commerce, Bachelor of Engineering, Bachelor of Computer Science) and some require need.

records.notes: SCOPE CORRECTION, stated plainly because the assigned award name does not exist as published. The assigned target was 'Dalhousie University International Scholarships'. No award of that name appears on dal.ca. Dalhousie does not publish a standalone international scholarship; it publishes one undergraduate entrance award programme, the General Entrance Award program (GEA), through which international students are considered for entrance scholarships and bursaries, and a parallel, separately published page for graduate international scholarships under the Faculty of Graduate Studies. The international-students page routes graduate applicants to that Faculty of Graduate Studies page and undergraduate applicants to financial aid for undergraduates, which is the separation that confirms this record's bachelor's level. This record therefore covers the GEA as the only broad international undergraduate funding instrument Dalhousie publishes. funding_amount is null on purpose: Dalhousie publishes a range, "$1K to $80K approximate range of award values yearly, and over 4 years", and per-award values rather than one programme amount, so no single CAD figure is claimed. Several named awards on the same page are restricted to Canadian high school graduates or Canadian citizens and are excluded from eligibility for an international applicant: Schulich Leader Scholarships (already indexed separately as id 312), Harrison McCain Scholarships (Canadian citizens or permanent residents), Bissett Scholarship (Cole Harbour High School), Fountain Performing Arts Undergraduate Scholarships and the Bachelor of Computer Science entrance scholarships (direct from high school, with the Leacross Women in Technology Scholarship the exception, which is open to Canadian and international applicants). Awards are credits against the student account, not a tuition waiver; tuition stays payable and the International Tuition Guarantee only fixes the fee at a guaranteed level. Contacts are drawn from the pages fetched, not guessed.

official_details.citizenship_residency: No citizenship, residency or international-status test is published for the programme as a whole. Dalhousie states flatly that "All students—domestic and international—are eligible to apply", and instructs international students to consider entrance awards "by submitting the General Entrance Award application". Individual named awards carry their own residency or nationality conditions, and several awards listed elsewhere on the same page are restricted to Canadian citizens, permanent residents or Canadian high school graduates and so are closed to an international applicant.
official_details.international_eligibility: Confirmed directly and explicitly. The Info for International Students page states that "Dalhousie offers more than 2,000 entrance awards (scholarships) each year, including scholarships and bursaries to support incoming students", that "Awards may be offered based on academics, achievements and involvement outside of the classroom, financial need or a combination of the above", and that "A general entrance award application is required to be considered". Its step-by-step international undergraduate pathway includes step 3, "Apply for scholarships: Take advantage of funding opportunities to support your studies by submitting your application for General Entrance Awards (GEA) through your Application Portal", with the note "GEA is applicable to students coming direct from high school if you apply by February 15." The Future undergraduate student awards page carries a dedicated "International students" section: "International students are considered for entrance awards by submitting the General Entrance Award application." International-specific documents are also addressed: a non-Canadian curriculum still requires Grade 12 first-semester marks, and where an Income Tax Notice of Assessment is unavailable, official government tax or income documents from the home country showing parent or guardian income, or an official employer letter, are accepted, with an English translation required if not in English or French. Several awards on the page are explicitly open only to Canadian students and do not reach an international applicant: Schulich Leader Scholarships (Canadian high school or CEGEP graduate and Canadian citizen), Harrison McCain Scholarships (Canadian citizens or permanent residents) and the Bissett Scholarship (Cole Harbour High School applicants). The Leacross Women in Technology Entrance Scholarship is explicitly open to "Canadian and international applicants".
official_details.study_mode: Full-time enrolment required to be paid: the award is applied only in the terms in which the student is "registered full-time (minimum 9 credit hours per term for degree students and 6 credit hours per term for technology students) at Dalhousie University for the term(s) in which the scholarship is awarded". The page publishes no part-time award route for the GEA programme.
official_details.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field or subject restriction at programme level: one GEA application considers the applicant across faculties and programmes. Named awards are programme-restricted, including Bachelor of Commerce (CorpFinance Indian Scholarship), Bachelor of Engineering with preference for Civil Engineering (Murray Family Jamaican Engineering Scholarship), Bachelor of Computer Science and Bachelor of Applied Computer Science (WeAreAllCS awards, Bachelor of Computer Science entrance scholarships, Leacross Women in Technology Entrance Scholarship), Bachelor of Commerce and Bachelor of Management (Faculty of Management Promise Scholarship for Black and Indigenous Students), Music and Theatre (Fountain Performing Arts Undergraduate Scholarships), and Architecture & Planning, Arts & Social Sciences, Computer Science, Engineering, Health and Management (Bissett Scholarship, which is also restricted to Cole Harbour High School applicants). Athletic scholarships are handled separately by Dalhousie Athletics via a prospective recruit form or direct contact with a coach. The International Tuition Guarantee, which fixes rather than funds tuition, covers only the Faculties of Agriculture, Arts & Social Sciences, Computer Science, Engineering, Management and Science.

If already accepted: complete the GEA application in the portal and submit an official first-semester transcript or provincial student ID number. If not yet accepted: apply to an undergraduate programme, complete the GEA application, pay the $70 CAD admissions application fee, and submit an official first-semester transcript or provincial student ID number. Applicants admitted on self-reported grades must additionally submit an official record of first-semester results. Financial or disability-related supporting documents are uploaded directly into the GEA application in the portal.

official_details.description: Dalhousie University's General Entrance Award program (GEA) is the single undergraduate entrance award route through which international students are considered for scholarships, bursaries and hybrid merit-and-need awards, and one of the 2,000+ entrance awards offered annually at an approximate yearly value range of $1K to $80K, one-time or renewable for up to 4 years. One application places the applicant in the pool for hundreds of awards, assessed individually on academic achievement, leadership and initiative, extracurricular involvement, community service, financial need and cultural identity, on the basis of Grade 12 first-semester final grades. Eligibility is open to domestic and international students alike, requires applying directly from high school or being a mature student with no transferable post-secondary study, requires Fall entry and the usual academic threshold, and excludes transfer students. The published cycle opened on October 1, 2026 and closes February 15, 2027. Awards are credited to the student account in two instalments in mid-August and mid-December against tuition and fees, with any residual refundable; tuition is not waived, there is no bond, and living, travel and immigration costs are not covered as published components.
official_details.coverage: A monetary award credit applied to the student account against tuition and fees in two equal instalments (mid-August, mid-December), one-time or renewable for up to 4 years, with residual funds over tuition and fees refundable. Not covered: any tuition waiver, a guaranteed living-cost component, residence and meal plan costs beyond residual credit, travel, study permit, eTA, visa and Provincial Attestation Letter costs.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are starting in the Fall term. Winter and Summer entry cannot use the GEA route; Dalhousie directs those students to current undergraduate student awards and bursaries instead.

Confirm you are applying directly from high school, or that you qualify as a mature student with no transferable post-secondary study. Transfer students are generally not eligible, and the only stated exception is Indigenous Black and First Nations students from the Maritimes seeking the FNIB Scholarship.
Check the cycle is live: the 2027-2028 GEA program opened October 1, 2026 and the deadline is February 15, 2027.
Have your Grade 12 first-semester final grades ready. If your school does not use semesters, first-half-of-year predicted or mid-term grades are acceptable.

Ask your school or issuing institution to send the transcript directly to admissions.documents@dal.ca. A transcript you upload yourself is not treated as official, and awards are not reassessed on later grades.

If your OUAC number or Nova Scotia Student ID number is already on file with Admissions you usually do not need to resend the transcript; check whether it already appears on your admission application status page, which is where transcripts are displayed, not in DalOnline.

If you have not yet been accepted: apply to an undergraduate programme and pay the $70 CAD admissions application fee as part of the award process. If you were admitted on self-reported grades, submit an official record of your first-semester results, because self-reported grades alone are not considered for the GEA programme.
Do not prepare reference letters, a resume, SAT/ACT scores or IELTS scores for the GEA application. None are required, and reference letters are not accepted for this programme.

If you need need-based support, upload financial or disability-related documents directly into the GEA application in the portal. Where an Income Tax Notice of Assessment is unavailable, use official government tax or income documents from your home country showing your parent or guardian income, or an official employer letter, with an English translation if not in English or French.

Review which of your awards are actually open to you. Schulich Leader Scholarships, Harrison McCain Scholarships and the Bissett Scholarship are closed to international applicants, and most separate-application awards are limited to students entering directly from Canadian high schools.

Plan the payment mechanics: the award lands on your student account in two equal instalments in mid-August and mid-December, and only registered full-time students (9 credit hours per term, 6 for technology) receive it.
If you are offered an early entrance award, be ready to pay your admission deposit by January 31 to lock it in.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the February 15 deadline. Dalhousie reviews applications after that date and gives no extension, and the date is fixed regardless of when the admission application was submitted.
Applying on self-reported grades only. Dalhousie states self-reported grades alone are not considered for the GEA programme, and awards are decided on Grade 12 first-semester final grades.
Uploading your own transcript instead of having the school send it to admissions.documents@dal.ca, which means it is not considered official.
Holding transferable post-secondary study. Transfer students are generally not eligible, and this cannot be waived after the fact.
Applying for Winter or Summer entry and assuming the GEA applies. Those intakes are directed to current student awards and bursaries.

Expecting IELTS or other language scores to improve the award outcome. The GEA application uses only the information in the GEA application, and IELTS scores are neither required nor considered for it.

Deferring admission without checking the rules. Deferral is limited to the winter term and requires an approved admission deferral, and completing transferable post-secondary study during the deferred year forfeits eligibility to re-apply.

alerts.message: The 2027-2028 General Entrance Award program closed its window on February 15, 2027. Dalhousie reviews applications after that date and notifies successful applicants in the spring, so a late application cannot be salvaged by an earlier admission submission.

If you were admitted using self-reported grades, Dalhousie states applications with self-reported grades alone will not be considered for the General Entrance Award program. You must submit an official record of your first-semester results.

Transfer students are generally not eligible for entrance awards, and the only stated exception is Indigenous Black and First Nations students from the Maritimes seeking the FNIB Scholarship. Holding transferable post-secondary study also ends any eligibility to re-apply after deferring.
The GEA route is Fall entry only. Students starting in winter or summer are directed to current undergraduate student awards and bursaries instead, which are a different pool with different terms.

Funds are applied only in terms in which you are registered full-time, a minimum of 9 credit hours per term for degree students or 6 credit hours per term for technology students. Reducing your course load silently stops the award for that term.

alerts.trigger: An award title that looks international but is not
alerts.message: Schulich Leader Scholarships require a Canadian high school or CEGEP graduation and Canadian citizenship, Harrison McCain Scholarships require Canadian citizenship or permanent residency, and the Bissett Scholarship is restricted to Cole Harbour High School applicants. Check the eligibility line on each award before planning around it.

This is an account credit against tuition and fees, not a fee waiver, and the International Tuition Guarantee only fixes the fee at a guaranteed level for six named faculties. Budget the full international fee and treat the award as an offset.

If you hold both a General Entrance Award and an Early Entrance Scholarship, Dalhousie keeps only the higher-value award. Early offers must be accepted by paying the admission deposit by January 31, and that guarantees no less than the early award amount.

alerts.trigger: Timing pressure after the award offer
alerts.message: After paying the admission deposit you receive a Provincial Attestation Letter that must be used for your study permit within 12 weeks. Build the immigration timeline backwards from the February 15 award deadline and the spring notification, not forwards from it.

submission_workflow: Submit your undergraduate admission application through the application portal at https://apply.dal.ca/apply/, paying the $70 CAD admissions application fee if you have not already paid one.
Complete the General Entrance Award application yourself in the same application portal. This single application is what puts you forward for hundreds of awards.
Ask your school or issuing institution to transmit your official Grade 12 first-semester transcript directly to admissions.documents@dal.ca. Do not rely on a self-uploaded copy.

Upload any financial or disability-related supporting documents directly inside the GEA application in the portal, and use home-country government income documents or an employer letter with an English translation if you have no Income Tax Notice of Assessment.
Verify everything is in before the February 15, 2027 deadline: Dalhousie states you must complete the application and submit all required documents before the deadline, and reviews only after it.
After the deadline, wait for notification in the spring; there is no published appeal process.
If you hold an early entrance award offer, pay your admission deposit by January 31 to guarantee no less than that early amount.
Accept your offer of admission and pay the deposit through the portal to secure the award, then expect the credit on your student account in two equal instalments in mid-August and mid-December.
Keep enrolment at full-time load every term the award is paid, so the 9 credit hour (or 6, technology) requirement is met and no instalment is withheld.

After the last day to add classes in each term, check whether a residual balance remains and request a refund from Student Accounts if you want the money sooner than term end; for urgent costs such as textbooks in the meantime, apply for an emergency loan.

records.name: International Brock Scholars Award
records.duration: Renewable. A student pursuing a four-year honours degree is eligible for a total of three renewals after the first-year award, giving a maximum of four years of funding; a student in a three-year pass degree is eligible for two renewals.
records.deadline: No separate scholarship application and therefore no separate scholarship deadline. The award is automatic: the International Brock Scholars Award is 'offered at the time of admission'. The only published deadline condition is that the student must 'Reply to your offer of admission by the deadline specified by the Registrar's Office' in order to confirm the award. The International Ambassador Award is the one award on the page that does require its own application, and it is marked '2026 Application Closed'.
records.application_period: There is no scholarship application window for the International Brock Scholars Award. It is assessed automatically from the admission average at the point an offer of admission is made, for each incoming international student entering a first undergraduate programme in the Fall term. Brock publishes the amount tiers on its 2026-2027 international students page, so the currently published figures are the 2026 entry amounts.
records.application_method: Automatic on admission. No application is required. Brock states: 'Brock Scholars awards are open to incoming students from anywhere in the world. To qualify, you must be entering your first undergraduate program in the Fall term (no previous post-secondary experience). No application is required.' The award is 'offered at the time of admission and may increase or decrease if your final average changes.' This is the opposite of the separate-application awards on the same pages, which are made by committee selection and require a dedicated application form, and of the OneApp, which is the route for hundreds of other Brock awards and bursaries.
records.description: The International Brock Scholars Award is Brock University's largest award and its main automatic entrance award for students from outside Canada. Brock states it is 'open to every incoming student from anywhere in the world' who is entering their first undergraduate programme in the Fall term with no previous post-secondary experience, and that 'No application is required'. The award is an academic distinction based on final admission average and carries a renewable financial component that is applied directly against tuition fees. Published 2026 first-year amounts for international students range from CAD $7,000 to CAD $32,000 depending on the final admission average, with renewal amounts of CAD $4,000 to CAD $20,000. Award amounts are described by the University as 'subject to annual approval by the Board of Trustees and are subject to change'.
records.best_fit: International applicants from any country who will enter their first undergraduate degree at Brock University in the Fall term with no previous post-secondary experience, and who reach a final admission average of at least 80 per cent. The maximum award requires a final admission average of 95 per cent or above. Applicants from the USA are not eligible for the international tiers; they qualify for the Domestic Brock Scholars Entrance Award instead. Students already holding a tuition waiver do not receive the tuition-offset component.
records.eligibility_summary: The applicant must be entering their first undergraduate programme at Brock University in the Fall term and must have no previous post-secondary experience. There is no citizenship or nationality restriction: the award is open to incoming students 'from anywhere in the world'. The award is set by final admission average, with a published minimum of 80 per cent for international students; below 80 per cent the applicant 'will no longer be eligible for a Brock Scholars award'. The admission average is calculated on the prerequisites for the offered programme of study, calculated to the nearest tenth of a percent and not rounded. Non-Ontario curricula are assessed by the Admissions Office and the criteria vary by curriculum. Students from the United States qualify only for the Domestic Brock Scholars Entrance Award amounts. Full-time study is required, with a minimum of 1.50 credits in each of the Fall and Winter terms.

records.selection_notes: There is no competition or committee selection for this award. Brock describes it as 'an academic distinction based on admission average grade', so selection is purely by final admission average against the published tiers. The award is offered at the time of admission and 'may increase or decrease if your final average changes'. Initial offers are made on secondary school grades available at the time of admission, and the offers are revised when final grades are submitted. The admission average is calculated using the prerequisites for the offered programme of study, to the nearest tenth of a percent, and Brock states 'We do not round averages up or down'. Renewal is separate and is assessed after each 5.0 credit milestone against the student's best 5.0 full credits, requiring a minimum 80 per cent average in each milestone, assessed at 5.0, 10.0 and 15.0 cumulative credits. No published selection weighting percentages beyond the average bands.
records.notes: Award selection: the assigned slot named 'Brock University International Scholarships', which is a family of awards rather than one award. Brock publishes several bachelor's-level awards open to incoming international students on one host. The International Brock Scholars Award was chosen because it is by far the best documented and the only one that is automatic rather than committee-selected: it is described by Brock as 'Our largest award', it publishes a full four-tier amount table with separate first-year and renewal figures, explicit admission-average criteria, renewal rules, course-load conditions and confirmation requirements. Other incoming-international awards on the same page were not recorded as separate records, so there is no duplicate-award conflict: the Brock Future Leaders Scholarship (CAD $10,000, 10 awards, committee selection, separate application), the International Curriculum awards (CAD $3,000, first 20 accepted international fee-paying students holding an international curriculum), the International Ambassador Award (variable, equal to domestic tuition rates, committee selection, and whose 2026 application is marked closed), the Brock Canadian High School Excellence Award (CAD $2,000, first 30 accepted international fee-paying students graduating from a Canadian high school), and the International Transfer Award (CAD $3,000, first 10 accepted international fee-paying transfers). The Caribbean International Scholarship (CAD $4,000) was deliberately NOT recorded as a candidate because Brock restricts it to a named list of Caribbean countries, which the research protocol lists as a hard-excluded region. Tuition coverage: the award is explicitly a partial tuition offset, applied directly to tuition fees, so tuition_coverage is true but fully_funded is false; there is no published living-cost component, and a student already holding a tuition waiver receives the distinction but not the tuition offset. No bond or service obligation is published. The Brock Future Leaders Scholarship application form is hosted on forms.office.com, a third-party form host, so that URL is not cited as an official source. logo_override is null pending a verified official-domain image; the brocku.ca pages lazy-load their logo behind a data: URI SVG placeholder, so the header image URL could not be read from the fetched markup.

official_details.application_cycle: Automatic admission-linked award for Fall entry each year. Brock publishes the international amount table on its 2026-2027 international students page, so the currently published tiers are the 2026 entry figures and are 'subject to annual approval by the Board of Trustees and are subject to change'. There is no scholarship application cycle because no application is required.
official_details.deadline_central_display: No separate scholarship deadline. The award is 'offered at the time of admission'. To keep it, the student must 'Reply to your offer of admission by the deadline specified by the Registrar's Office'.
official_details.deadline_note: No exact calendar date is published for this award and none has been invented. Brock publishes no scholarship application deadline because there is no scholarship application: the award is automatic and 'offered at the time of admission'. The only date-bearing instruction in the published terms is the confirmation requirement to 'Reply to your offer of admission by the deadline specified by the Registrar's Office', and Brock does not publish that date on the scholarship pages; it is programme- and term-specific and is published by the Registrar's Office. A related hard date is published for transcripts rather than for the award: Brock states that official transcripts 'will only be accepted until Oct. 31' for scholarship revisions.
official_details.status_note: The award is open because it has no application window to close: Brock states the awards are 'open to every incoming student from anywhere in the world' and that 'No application is required'. At the verification date of 2026-10-03 Brock's published amount tables are the 2026-2027 entry figures, and the page footer carries a 2026 copyright. The one separate-application international award on the same page, the International Ambassador Award, is marked '2026 Application Closed', which confirms that the automatic award itself remains open for current applicants.
official_details.funding_duration: Renewable. Three renewals in a four-year honours degree (maximum four years of funding in total) or two renewals in a three-year pass degree.
official_details.tuition_coverage_note: The award is applied against tuition, not paid as an unrestricted stipend. Brock states that the award 'currently includes a renewable financial component to partially offset tuition fees' and that 'Your scholarship will be applied directly to your tuition fees. This will take place before classes begin in September, reducing the amount you owe to the University.' tuition_coverage is therefore true in the sense that the money directly reduces tuition. However the University explicitly calls it a partial offset, the published maximum of CAD $32,000 is a fraction of a full international tuition load, and no tuition-fee waiver, living-cost, residence or travel component is published, so fully_funded is false. Two published limits apply: scholarships 'cannot be used for first instalments or down payments', and 'students already holding a tuition waiver will have the academic distinction noted on their transcript but will not receive the tuition offset funding'.

Applied directly against tuition as a partial offset; renewable for up to three further years. Not full funding, and no living-cost component is published.

official_details.description: The International Brock Scholars Award is Brock University's largest award and its automatic entrance award for students from outside Canada. Brock states that it is 'open to every incoming student from anywhere in the world', requiring only that the student be entering their first undergraduate programme in the Fall term with no previous post-secondary experience, and that 'No application is required'. The award is an academic distinction based on final admission average and carries a renewable financial component that partially offsets tuition fees and is applied directly against them before classes begin in September. Published 2026 first-year amounts range from CAD $7,000 to CAD $32,000, with renewal amounts from CAD $4,000 to CAD $20,000. Award amounts are subject to annual approval by the Board of Trustees and are subject to change.
official_details.coverage: A renewable tuition offset for incoming international undergraduates, tiered by final admission average: first-year amounts of CAD $32,000, CAD $24,000, CAD $12,500 or CAD $7,000, and renewal amounts of CAD $20,000, CAD $15,000, CAD $8,000 or CAD $4,000. The money is applied directly to tuition fees. It is explicitly a partial offset rather than full tuition, and no living-cost, residence, meal, travel or health component is published for this award.

application_readiness_checklist: Do not look for a scholarship form. This award is automatic: Brock states 'No application is required', so the only thing you submit is an undergraduate admission application as an international fee-paying student

Aim for a final admission average of at least 80 per cent, because below that 'you will no longer be eligible for a Brock Scholars award'; the tiers at 95.0 and above, 90.0-94.9, 85.0-89.9 and 80.0-84.9 are worth very different amounts
Make sure you are entering your first undergraduate programme in the Fall term with no previous post-secondary experience, since both conditions are required to qualify
If you are applying from the United States, check the domestic award instead; Brock states 'U.S.A. applicants will only qualify for Domestic Brock Scholars Award amounts'
If you already hold a Brock tuition waiver, understand that you receive the academic distinction but not the tuition offset funding, because Brock states those two are mutually exclusive

Reply to your offer of admission by the Registrar's Office deadline, since confirming the scholarship requires it alongside the name, programme, year of study and likeness release, and full-time registration
Register a full-time course load of at least 1.50 credits in each of the Fall and Winter terms, because reducing to part-time pro-rates or withdraws the award
Watch the transcript cut-off. Brock states official transcripts 'will only be accepted until Oct. 31' for scholarship revisions, and summer courses taken after graduation will be used in the revision

If you are a co-op student, complete the Brock Scholars Award Renewal Form so that your renewal is reviewed, and note that work-term additive credit courses used for the co-op certification are excluded from the milestone calculation
If you are in a three-year pass degree, plan for two renewals rather than three; honours degrees of four years get three
If you intend to apply for OSAP, do not list this scholarship under Award Income in the OSAP application, because Brock reports it on your behalf
common_rejection_risks: Hunting for a scholarship application that does not exist and assuming there is a deadline to meet; this award requires no application at all
A final admission average below 80 per cent, which ends eligibility entirely rather than reducing the tier
A final average that lands below the band offered on the provisional offer, because Brock states the award 'may increase or decrease if your final average changes'
Applicants with previous post-secondary experience, who are excluded because the award requires entering a first undergraduate programme
Applying from the USA and expecting the international tiers, which Brock says are unavailable to USA applicants
Missing the Registrar's Office reply deadline for the admission offer, which is the only step that confirms the scholarship
Dropping below a full-time course load, which causes the tuition offset or scholarship to be pro-rated or withdrawn
Falling under 80 per cent in a 5.0 credit milestone and losing the renewal
Expecting the award to pay living costs, housing or travel; it is a tuition-only partial offset
Relying on it to cover a first instalment or down payment, which Brock explicitly excludes
estimated_uncovered_costs: The majority of international tuition fees. Even the top tier of CAD $32,000 in year 1 is only a partial offset and the University describes it as 'a renewable financial component to partially offset tuition fees'
All renewal tuition above CAD $20,000 per year at the top tier, and above CAD $15,000, CAD $8,000 or CAD $4,000 at the lower tiers
Non-instructional and other program-related fees; the award is applied to tuition and no separate fee coverage is published
Residence and meal plan costs, for which no coverage is published on the award page
Books and supplies

Health insurance. Brock publishes Universal Health Insurance Plan (UHIP) as mandatory health insurance coverage for all international students, plus a BUSU Health and Dental Plan described as a mandatory fee for all international students, and an International recovery fee of CAD $750 charged by the Province of Ontario to all international students at public colleges and universities
Any tuition instalment or down payment, which the scholarship cannot be used for
Study permit fees, travel to Canada and other arrival costs not named in the published provision
document_audit: Confirm your Brock admission application was submitted as an international fee-paying student, since the international tiers do not apply otherwise
Track the Oct. 31 cut-off for official transcripts so that any scholarship revision based on final grades is processed
Keep your final admission average to one decimal place in mind, because Brock calculates to the nearest tenth of a percent and states 'We do not round averages up or down'

If you took a non-Ontario curriculum, get your Admissions Office assessment of how your final average is computed, because Brock states the criteria 'will vary by curriculum, and will be determined by the Admissions Office'
For co-op students, ensure the Brock Scholars Award Renewal Form is filed, since renewal is otherwise not reviewed

alerts.message: Brock accepts official transcripts only until Oct. 31 for scholarship revisions. Late transcripts will not change the award figure.

Reply to your offer of admission by the Registrar's Office deadline, agree to the name, programme, year of study and likeness release, and register full time. That is what confirms the scholarship.
Award amounts are subject to annual approval by the Board of Trustees and are subject to change, so the figures published for 2026 entry are not a guarantee for later entry.
Renewal is assessed at 5.0, 10.0 and 15.0 cumulative credits against your best 5.0 full credits, and requires at least 80 per cent in each milestone.

submission_workflow: Apply for admission to a Brock University undergraduate programme as an international fee-paying student
Receive the offer of admission carrying the Brock Scholars Award, calculated from the admission average of the prerequisites for your offered programme
Reply to the offer of admission by the Registrar's Office deadline, agree to the release of your name, programme, year of study and likeness, and register a full-time course load
Submit final official transcripts by Oct. 31 if the award figure needs revising
Study full time, at least 1.50 credits in each of the Fall and Winter terms
At each 5.0 credit milestone, achieve at least 80 per cent to have the award renewed, and file the renewal form if you are a co-op student

records.description: The University of Windsor awards scholarships and awards to international students to recognise academic achievement. The International Student Centre states that "Awards provided to entering undergraduates include the International Student Entrance Awards/Scholarships, the Outstanding Scholars Award, and the University of Windsor Women in Engineering Award," and that "These awards are made at the time of admission. No additional application is required." The award recorded here is the International Student Entrance Awards/Scholarships for entering undergraduates, the other two named awards being separately identified by the University and not folded into this record. The University also states that international students "may also earn in-course awards while continuing their studies," and separately that students entering research-based graduate programmes meeting the equivalent of a Canadian 80% "will be considered for a graduate study scholarship." No monetary value has yet been read from an official page for this interim write.

Because the award is made at the time of admission with no additional application, it fits applicants who are pursuing admission to Windsor on academic grounds rather than applicants seeking a separate funding competition. Not suitable as a route for in-course funding, which the University handles through separately published in-course awards and bursaries, or for graduate study, which the University treats as a separate scholarship route.
records.eligibility_summary: Eligibility follows the admission decision rather than a separate scholarship competition. The award therefore attaches to an offer of admission to an undergraduate programme, with academic achievement the stated basis on which the University provides scholarships and awards to international students: "The University of Windsor provides to international students scholarships and awards to recognize academic achievement." Detailed selection conditions, grade thresholds, award values, renewal requirements and holder conditions are published by the University in its entrance awards regulations and on its Student Awards and Financial Aid pages, which were not read for this interim write and are therefore not asserted here.

application_readiness_checklist: Apply for admission to an undergraduate programme at the University of Windsor as an international student. There is no separate scholarship application to submit, because the University states the awards to entering undergraduates "are made at the time of admission. No additional application is required."
Target admission intake for the year you intend to enter. The award attaches to the admission decision, so admission timing, not a scholarship deadline, is what matters.

Read the University's own entrance awards regulations for the year of entry before you rely on any value or grade threshold, because the award's value is set by the regulations for the relevant academic year.

Check whether the Outstanding Scholars Award or the University of Windsor Women in Engineering Award applies to you as well, since the University names them as separate awards for entering undergraduates.
Treat the Study in Canada Scholarship as a separate track: the University states Global Affairs Canada provides it but that the University must submit the application on your behalf.

Assuming an admission offer automatically includes an award. The University states the awards are made at the time of admission, but it does not state that every admitted international undergraduate receives one.

Planning finances on an assumed amount. No value was read from an official page in this research, so any figure in circulation should be verified against the University's current entrance awards regulations.
Applying as a continuing student rather than an entering one, since this is an entrance award and in-course funding runs through separate awards and bursaries.
Confusing this record with the Outstanding Scholars Award or the Women in Engineering Award, which the University names as distinct awards.
Missing that donor-sponsored and special event awards may not follow the standard deferral rules, so deferring admission can affect a related award.
