records.duration: For the entire duration of the course; the reduction is applied at the commencement of each session for as long as the recipient remains enrolled and meets the conditions. CSU publishes no fixed number of years, because it depends on the degree programme.
records.deadline: Applications open; Closes: 11:59pm 31 Dec 2026. The How to Apply section separately states 'Applications are open until further advice.'
records.application_period: Rolling: applications are open and assessed as part of the course admissions process, with the award page stating a closing date of 11:59pm 31 Dec 2026 and also that applications are open until further advice. CSU does not publish intake-by-intake scholarship windows for this award.
records.application_method: Automatic on admission. There is no separate scholarship application: 'Your application for this scholarship will be automatically considered by our admissions team when you apply for an eligible course on an eligible campus' and 'There is no additional application process.' The outcome is advised with the offer letter, and the award appears on the offer letter.
records.description: The International Student Merit Scholarship is a Charles Sturt University tuition-fee reduction for new commencing international students. It provides a 25% fee discount for the entire duration of the course, deducted from tuition fees at the commencement of each session. It is awarded automatically by the admissions team when an applicant applies for an eligible course in internal/on-campus mode at an eligible campus; there is no separate application form and the outcome is advised with the offer letter. Academic entry is assessed either through an Australian AQF Level 7 route or through published Year 12 equivalent percentage thresholds of 75% for most undergraduate degrees and 85% for Allied Health courses other than Nursing.
records.best_fit: New international applicants to Charles Sturt University who are commencing an approved on-campus undergraduate degree at an eligible regional or metropolitan campus and who can meet a published Year 12 equivalent academic entry score. Not suitable for continuing students, transfer students from another CSU course, online-mode starters, international exchange or study abroad students, or students already holding an Australia Awards or Research Training Program scholarship.
records.funding_period: per academic session, for the duration of the course
records.eligibility_summary: Open to new commencing international applicants studying an approved course in internal/on-campus mode at the Albury-Wodonga, Bathurst, Dubbo, Melbourne, Orange, Port Macquarie, Sydney or Wagga Wagga campuses. Not available to continuing or transferring students, international exchange or study abroad applicants, students commencing an online-mode course, students commencing at a CSU international partner, or students holding an Australia Awards or Research Training Program scholarship. Applicants must satisfy one of two published academic routes: an Australian academic progression route (AQF Level 7 or above completed in Australia within 12 months of course commencement) or a general academic route requiring 85 per cent in equivalent Australian Year 12 for an eligible Allied Health course other than Nursing, 75 per cent for any other eligible undergraduate degree, or 65 per cent for an eligible postgraduate degree. The scholarship is assessed as part of the admissions process and cannot be held together with another Charles Sturt-funded tuition fee scholarship.
eligibility: Be a new commencing international applicant for an approved course offered by Charles Sturt University.
Study in internal/on-campus mode at an eligible campus (Albury-Wodonga, Bathurst, Dubbo, Melbourne, Orange, Port Macquarie, Sydney or Wagga Wagga).
Not be a continuing or transferring student, and not transfer from another Charles Sturt course.
Not be an International Exchange or Study Abroad applicant.
Not be commencing an online-mode course or a course at a Charles Sturt international partner.
Not already hold an Australia Awards or Research Training Program (RTP) scholarship.
Satisfy one of the two published academic criteria: the Australian academic progression route, or the general academic entry-score route.

Australian academic progression route: have completed an Australian AQF Level 7 or higher qualification in Australia, offshore or online, with the completion date within 12 months of the applied course commencement date, and be new to CSU or new to that level of study.

General academic route: academic entry score of 85 per cent in equivalent Australian Year 12 for an eligible Allied Health course except Nursing, 75 per cent for any other eligible undergraduate degree, or 65 per cent in equivalent Australian undergraduate study for an eligible postgraduate degree.
Enrol in a course from the published list of approved undergraduate or postgraduate courses with the matching entry-score threshold.
Meet the Genuine Student requirement, including financial capacity, and pay the appropriate fee deposit to receive a Confirmation of Enrolment (e-COE).
coverage: A 25% reduction in tuition fees, applied for the entire duration of the course and deducted from tuition fees at the commencement of each session while the conditions are met.
benefits: 25% tuition fee reduction for the duration of the course.
Automatic consideration: no separate scholarship application is required.
Award confirmed in the offer letter issued with the admission offer.
May be deferred to a future intake and still be awarded.
May be transferred to another campus provided the student remains in the same course and meets the criteria.
An Approved Leave of Absence does not terminate the scholarship.
requirements: Apply for admission to an approved Charles Sturt University course in internal/on-campus mode at an eligible campus; this single application is also the scholarship application.
Satisfy the published academic entry score for the specific approved course.
Accept the offer of study at the university and make the appropriate fee deposit to receive a e-COE.
Continue to meet the Genuine Student requirements, including financial capacity.
Maintain satisfactory academic progress and continued enrolment to keep the scholarship active.
Do not hold another Charles Sturt-funded tuition fee scholarship concurrently.
Sign a media release authorising the use of your photographs and images for promotional and marketing purposes, and agree to provide information, testimonials and promotional content.
required_documents: Admission application to an approved CSU course in internal/on-campus mode at an eligible campus, submitted through the normal admissions process (the scholarship itself requires no separate document set).
Evidence of the academic entry score for the approved course, assessed by CSU against the published Year 12 equivalent thresholds.

CSU states it will 'award as many scholarships as possible, with an intent to reward every eligible student', so the academic entry threshold is the operative filter rather than a ranked competition. The scholarship outcome is advised with the offer letter.

official_details.description: The International Student Merit Scholarship is a Charles Sturt University tuition-fee reduction for new commencing international students, valued at a 25% fee discount for the entire duration of the course and deducted from tuition fees at the commencement of each session. It is awarded automatically by the admissions team when an applicant applies for an approved course in internal/on-campus mode at an eligible campus, with no separate application process, and the outcome is advised with the offer letter. Academic entry is assessed either through an Australian AQF Level 7 progression route or through published Year 12 equivalent thresholds of 75 per cent for most undergraduate degrees and 85 per cent for Allied Health courses other than Nursing. There is no bond, no living-cost component and no travel component.
official_details.coverage: Covers a 25% reduction in tuition fees for the entire duration of the course, deducted from tuition fees at the commencement of each session. Does not cover the remaining 75% of tuition, accommodation, living costs, travel, visa or the e-COE, and no bond attaches to the award.

application_readiness_checklist: Pick your course from CSU's published list of approved courses and check the entry-score threshold attached to it before you apply: 75 per cent Year 12 equivalent for most undergraduate degrees, 85 per cent for Allied Health except Nursing.

Apply to an approved course in internal/on-campus mode at Albury-Wodonga, Bathurst, Dubbo, Melbourne, Orange, Port Macquarie, Sydney or Wagga Wagga. Do not rely on an online-mode offer, which is expressly ineligible.
No separate scholarship form exists. Your CSU admission application is the scholarship application, so do not spend time hunting for a scholarship portal.

If you are relying on the Australian academic progression route, have your AQF Level 7 or above completion certificate and date ready, and make sure the completion date is within 12 months of your course commencement date.
Keep the offer letter, because the scholarship decision travels with it, and pay the fee deposit promptly so the e-COE is issued.
Budget for the remaining 75% of tuition plus accommodation, living costs, travel and visa yourself: this award is a fee discount, not a funded place.
Read the promotional conditions before you accept: you will be expected to join the student body, give testimonials, be photographed, and sign a media release.
Do not accept another Charles Sturt-funded tuition fee scholarship alongside this one, and do not assume it can be combined with a CSU-funded award.
common_rejection_risks: Applying for an online-mode course, which is expressly excluded from the scholarship even though CSU offers online degrees.
Applying through a CSU international partner rather than to a CSU campus, which is also excluded.
Missing the academic entry threshold for the specific approved course, where Allied Health and most other undergraduate degrees carry different thresholds.

Being a continuing student, or transferring from another CSU course or applying with advanced standing without confirming eligibility first; the page excludes transferring students while noting that some advanced-standing cases are still treated as commencing.
Holding an Australia Awards or Research Training Program scholarship, which disqualifies the applicant from this award.
Submitting through an exchange or study abroad channel rather than a degree admission.
Accepting a second CSU-funded tuition fee scholarship, which terminates eligibility for this one.
Missing the 11:59pm 31 Dec 2026 cut-off, since assessment runs through the admissions process and late offers may fall outside the published window.
estimated_uncovered_costs: The remaining 75% of tuition fees for every session of the course; the award is a partial remission only.

records.description: The John Curtin Global Excellence Scholarship is a merit-based award funded by Curtin University for international, fee-paying, non-sponsored students enrolling in an eligible undergraduate degree or Master degree by coursework at a Curtin Western Australian campus, commencing in 2027 or 2028. Curtin states that the scholarship 'Only covers tuition fees and does not cover any other international student expense', is credited to the recipient's fee account after the census date of the first study period, and cannot be withdrawn or refunded in cash. There is no separate scholarship application: every qualifying application to Curtin is assessed automatically and the outcome is confirmed by a supplementary letter issued with the Letter of Offer.

records.selection_notes: There is no separate application or separate selection panel. Curtin states that 'All qualifying applications to Curtin are automatically assessed for the John Curtin Global Excellence Scholarship' and that Global Admissions will assess each application accordingly and issue a supplementary letter with the Letter of Offer to confirm whether the applicant has been successful. The published academic threshold for entry is a Course-Weighted Average of 95% or equivalent in the most recent and eligible course of study, which Curtin determines and may change without notice. No selection weighting, panel, interview or shortlisting process is published. Curtin reserves the right to cease offering the Scholarship when all Scholarship places are filled, so the published closing date is not a guarantee that places remain.

official_details.application_cycle: Annual award, named by commencement year. Applications for the scholarship are open from 27 July 2026 and close on 1 October 2027, and the scholarship is awarded for study commencing in 2027 or 2028 at a Curtin Western Australian campus. Because there is no separate scholarship application, candidates apply on the Curtin course application cycle for the relevant intake.
official_details.deadline_central_display: Applications close 1/10/2027 (Curtin day/month/year format, so 1 October 2027), with applications opening 27/07/2026 (27 July 2026). Curtin publishes no time of day for this closing date.
official_details.deadline_note: This is the scholarship's own published closing date and it is exact: 1 October 2027, Australia/Perth (AWST, UTC+8). No time of day is published, so deadline_precision is 'day'. Two caveats are recorded rather than resolved. First, Curtin reserves the right to cease offering the Scholarship when all Scholarship places are filled, so the published date is not a guarantee that a place remains. Second, because assessment is automatic on the Curtin course application, the binding constraint for any individual applicant is the course application closing date for the chosen intake, which differs by course and by intake. The Curtin application deadlines page was read but it served the domestic visitor view, in which Semester 1 2027 applications 'opened on Friday 1 May 2026, and will close for most courses on Thursday 28 January 2027'. The international-view deadline for the specific intake a non-domestic applicant would use was therefore not captured, so no institutional deadline is asserted here.

official_details.funding_period: 40% of the tuition fee of the course, credited for up to 4 years for an undergraduate degree course or a maximum of 2 years for a Master's degree by coursework, across the scholarship term
official_details.funding_duration: Up to 4 years for an undergraduate degree course; a maximum of 2 years for a Master degree by coursework. This is the scholarship term.
official_details.tuition_coverage_note: The award is a tuition fee reduction and does cover tuition fees, but only partially: 40% off the tuition fee of the course, credited for up to 4 years for an undergraduate degree course or a maximum of 2 years for a Master's degree by coursework, against all units enrolled within the scholarship term. Curtin is explicit that it 'Only covers tuition fees and does not cover any other international student expense', so the recipient still pays the remaining 60% of tuition fees plus the full Deposit stated in the Letter of Offer. It is also explicit that the award 'Cannot be withdrawn or refunded in cash' and cannot be transferred to a Curtin campus or partner outside Western Australia or to another university. Because it is tuition-only and leaves 60% of tuition and all living costs payable, fully_funded is false.

official_details.description: The John Curtin Global Excellence Scholarship is a merit-based scholarship funded by Curtin University. Eligible students receive 40% off the tuition fee of the course they are undertaking, credited for up to 4 years for an undergraduate degree course or a maximum of 2 years for a Master degree by coursework, as a tuition fee credit against all units enrolled within the course within the scholarship term. It is open to international, fee-paying, non-sponsored students of any nationality except Australian who will study at a Curtin Western Australian campus commencing in 2027 or 2028, and who have achieved a Course-Weighted Average of 95% or equivalent in their most recent and eligible course of study. The scholarship is credited to the recipient's fee account after the census date of the first study period, only covers tuition fees, and cannot be withdrawn or refunded in cash. There is no separate scholarship application: all qualifying applications to Curtin are assessed automatically and Global Admissions confirms the outcome by issuing a supplementary letter with the Letter of Offer.
official_details.coverage: 40% of the tuition fee of the course, credited for up to 4 years for an undergraduate degree course or a maximum of 2 years for a Master degree by coursework. Tuition fees only; no living cost, accommodation, travel or other international student expense is covered.

records.name: Johns Hopkins International Scholarships
records.program_type: University need-based grant and merit scholarship for international undergraduates
records.duration: Typically four years; need-based aid awarded in the first year renews automatically in later years
records.deadline: Financial Aid Deadline: November 15, 2026 for Early Decision I; January 15, 2027 for Early Decision II and Regular Decision; March 15, 2027 for transfer. Updated dates are made public in August each year.
records.application_period: 2027 entry cycle. Early Decision I application deadline 1 November 2026 with financial aid deadline 15 November 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision application deadline 2 January 2027 with financial aid deadline 15 January 2027; transfer application deadline 1 March 2027 with financial aid deadline 15 March 2027. The Application Deadlines & Requirements page states that updated dates are made public in August each year.
records.application_method: Merit scholarships are automatic on admission: all applicants are automatically considered for merit scholarships when they apply, no separate application is required, and recipients are notified at the time of the admissions decision. Need-based aid requires a separate, mandatory step: the applicant must indicate an interest in financial aid on the admissions application and submit both the International Student Certification of Finances (COF) and the CSS Profile by the financial aid deadline of the chosen plan. No separate application exists for international applicants beyond the standard admissions application.
records.description: Johns Hopkins is need-aware for international students rather than need-blind, meaning a family's financial circumstances are considered in the admissions process. For admitted international citizens admitted in Early Decision I, Early Decision II and Regular Decision, Hopkins promises to meet 100% of a family's demonstrated need without any loans, using need-based scholarships that do not need to be paid back. About 10% of international students receive financial aid, and Hopkins offers a small number of merit scholarships to international citizens each year, for which all applicants are automatically considered with no additional application. Aid must be requested as a first-year applicant, and Hopkins does not currently offer financial aid to international transfer students.
records.best_fit: International first-year applicants who are not U.S. citizens, permanent residents, eligible noncitizens or DACA/undocumented holders, and whose families can show a lower ability to pay. International transfer students are not eligible for Hopkins financial aid, so this applies only to first-year entry.
records.eligibility_summary: Eligibility is open to applicants who are not U.S. citizens, permanent residents, eligible noncitizens or DACA/undocumented holders, including citizens of another country attending secondary school in the U.S. Aid is limited: about 10% of international students receive financial aid, and Hopkins awards only a small number of merit scholarships to international citizens each year. Aid must be requested as a first-year applicant; international students who do not apply for financial aid as first-year applicants can never apply for aid later, and international students cannot apply for financial aid after admissions decisions are released. Hopkins does not currently offer financial aid to international transfer students. International citizens are eligible for merit scholarships in all admissions plans and receive the same financial aid consideration in each.

records.selection_notes: Merit scholarships are based on academic and personal achievement both in and outside the classroom; all applicants are automatically considered when they apply, regardless of citizenship or ability to pay, and selected recipients are notified with the admissions decision. Need-based scholarships are based solely on a family's ability to pay for college. Because Hopkins is need-aware for international citizens, financial circumstances are considered in the admissions process itself. Applicants in all admissions plans receive the same consideration for financial aid. Hopkins publishes no numerical weighting for either component.

official_details.funding_duration: Typically four years of undergraduate study. official_details.tuition_coverage_note: For recipients, tuition is covered: Hopkins promises to meet 100% of a family's demonstrated need without any loans for international citizens admitted in Early Decision I, Early Decision II and Regular Decision, and publishes that families making up to $200,000 pay no tuition. fully_funded is nevertheless false because three limits remain. First, the award is need-based and selective: only about 10% of international students receive financial aid and merit scholarships to international citizens are a small number each year, so admission does not confer funding. Second, it meets demonstrated need rather than the full cost of attendance, so the family must still contribute what it can pay and the amount varies with need and can change year to year. Third, international students are ineligible for Title IV federal aid and state aid, so no federal or state grant can top up a shortfall, and work-study is a separate opportunity rather than part of this award.

official_details.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants who are neither U.S. citizens nor permanent residents, eligible noncitizens, nor holders of DACA or undocumented status. Applicants holding an F-1, F-2, M-1, J-1, J-2, G-series, A-2/A-3, NATO, B-1/B-2, H-series, L-series or U visa, and who do not have DACA or undocumented status, are international applicants at Hopkins.
official_details.international_eligibility: International students are eligible for both need-based and merit scholarships, although Hopkins states both types of assistance are limited. Hopkins is need-aware for international students, meaning financial circumstances are considered in the admissions process, whereas it is need-blind for domestic applicants. For all international citizens admitted in Early Decision I, Early Decision II and Regular Decision, Hopkins promises to meet 100% of a family's demonstrated need without any loans, using need-based scholarships that do not need to be paid back. About 10% of international students receive financial aid, and a small number of merit scholarships are awarded to international citizens each year. All international applicants must submit the Certification of Finances; those seeking aid must also submit the CSS Profile. Hopkins does not currently offer financial aid to international transfer students, and international students are ineligible for federal and state aid.
official_details.application_method: Merit scholarships are automatic on admission: every applicant is automatically considered for merit scholarships when applying, no separate application is required, and recipients are notified at the time of the admissions decision. Need-based aid requires a separate, mandatory financial aid step: the applicant must indicate an interest in financial aid on the admissions application and submit the International Student Certification of Finances plus the CSS Profile (or the free JHU ISFAA alternative) by the financial aid deadline of the chosen admissions plan. There is no separate application for international applicants beyond the standard admissions application, and international students cannot apply for financial aid after admissions decisions are released.

official_details.description: Johns Hopkins University is need-aware for international students and promises to meet 100% of a family's demonstrated need without any loans for international citizens admitted in Early Decision I, Early Decision II and Regular Decision, using need-based scholarships that do not need to be paid back. About 10% of international students receive financial aid. Hopkins also awards a small number of merit scholarships each year on academic and personal achievement, for which international citizens are eligible in all admissions plans and are automatically considered with no separate application. Need-based aid requires the applicant to indicate an interest in financial aid on the admissions application and to submit the CSS Profile and International Student Certification of Finances by the financial aid deadline.
official_details.program_type: University need-based grant and merit scholarship for international undergraduates
official_details.coverage: Meets 100% of a family's demonstrated need, defined as the difference between the total cost of attendance each year and what a family can pay, without any loans and using grants that do not need to be paid back. The award amount varies with financial need and can change year to year if household or financial circumstances change. Hopkins also states that families making up to $200,000 pay no tuition. Federal Pell, FSEOG and state aid are listed on the same pages but are FAFSA-based and unavailable to international students, and work-study is a separate opportunity.

application_readiness_checklist: Decide your admissions plan early: the financial aid deadline (15 November 2026 for ED I, 15 January 2027 for ED II and Regular Decision) is later than the admissions deadline, and both are hard cutoffs
Confirm you are classified as an international applicant, since that classification determines both the Certification of Finances requirement and need-aware review
Indicate an interest in financial aid on the admissions application in the first year if you may need any assistance during the degree, because there is no later route to aid
Submit the Certification of Finances through the applicant portal as soon as the admissions application is submitted, since the form is generated there and every international applicant needs it
Submit the CSS Profile by the plan's financial aid deadline, or start the free JHU ISFAA alternative and allow the stated 5 to 7 days of processing time
Plan for a budget review of your family's income, assets and unusual circumstances before the CSS Profile, since need-based aid is determined solely from what a family can pay
Do not count on federal aid: international students are ineligible for Title IV funds, Pell and FSEOG
Have your school counselor send the secondary school report and arrange two teacher evaluations from different subject teachers
Block out mid-February for the mid-year school report request that arrives by email
If applying Early Decision I or II, arrange parent/guardian and counselor signatures for the binding Early Decision Agreement well before the deadline
common_rejection_risks: Missing the financial aid deadline rather than the admissions deadline, which voids the aid application
Failing to submit the Certification of Finances, which leaves the application incomplete for every international applicant regardless of aid request
Not indicating an interest in financial aid in the first year, after which aid is never available
Attempting to apply for need-based aid after the admissions decision is released, which Hopkins does not permit
Relying on a nonexistent CSS fee waiver; Hopkins does not issue them for international applicants, so the free JHU ISFAA is the fallback
Expecting admission to bring funding: only about 10% of international students receive aid, and merit awards to international citizens are a small number each year
Assuming need-blind treatment; Hopkins is need-aware for international students, so financial circumstances affect the admissions process itself
Applying as a transfer student and expecting aid, which Hopkins does not offer to international transfers
Underestimating the aid cliff: need is recalculated annually, so a family income increase can reduce the award in a later year
Omitting a verified English translation with non-English school documents
estimated_uncovered_costs: The family's own assessed contribution, because the award meets demonstrated need rather than the full cost of attendance
Whatever sits outside the cost of attendance calculation and is therefore not covered, such as international airfare, visa and immigration fees, and travel home
Books, supplies and personal expenses not covered by demonstrated need
Private education loans for international transfer students, where most lenders require a U.S. citizen co-signer and Hopkins includes no loans in its offers
Any gap created by an increase in family income or assets in a later year, since the award amount is recalculated each year

records.name: Middlebury College Financial Aid for International Students
records.duration: Full duration of the enrolled bachelor's degree; the official pages publish no separate award term
records.deadline: Financial aid application deadlines for the 2027-2028 academic year: November 1, 2026 (Posse Scholar), November 15, 2026 (Early Decision I), December 1, 2026 (QuestBridge), January 3, 2027 (Early Decision II), February 1, 2027 (Regular Decision), March 1, 2027 (Fall 2027 Transfer) and November 1, 2027 (Spring 2028 Transfer)
records.application_period: 2027-2028 academic year aid cycle: the CSS Profile and FAFSA deadlines are November 1, 2026 (Posse Scholar), November 15, 2026 (Early Decision I), December 1, 2026 (QuestBridge), January 3, 2027 (Early Decision II), February 1, 2027 (Regular Decision), March 1, 2027 (Fall 2027 Transfer) and November 1, 2027 (Spring 2028 Transfer). The admissions application itself is due November 2 for Early Decision I and January 4 for Early Decision II and Regular Decision, so the aid deadline is the binding one for this award.
records.application_method: Not a separate scholarship application. Aid is awarded automatically within the admission process: the applicant submits the Common Application, Coalition Application, or QuestBridge Application and files Middlebury's financial aid application, the CSS Profile being required for every prospective undergraduate applying for aid and mandatory for international students, with the FAFSA additionally required for US citizens and eligible noncitizens. Aid must be applied for by the published financial aid deadline; the College states it is need aware in the admission of international students and that applicants seeking financial assistance must apply for aid when they apply for admission. The final offer is issued in early summer after Middlebury verifies the financial aid application of every undergraduate who enrolls, and is viewed in the Middlebury Financial Aid Portal.
records.description: Middlebury College publishes no single named international scholarship; the funding it publishes for international undergraduates is need-based institutional financial aid, and the College states that if you are an undergraduate student admitted to Middlebury, it will meet your full demonstrated financial need, with almost all of its aid being institutional grants and scholarships that do not have to be repaid. Published figures are institutional rather than award-specific: $80M institutional aid awarded, 50% of students receiving aid, 100% calculated need met, a $66K average grant, and 100% need-based aid. For international applicants the College states it is need aware, so assistance must be requested when applying for admission, the CSS Profile is required for all prospective undergraduates filing for aid and is the only accepted international route, and the College does not accept the ISFAA or a paper CSS Profile. Aid includes all books and supplies, higher-need students also qualify for student health insurance and a new laptop, and the College states it is tuition-free for families with annual incomes up to $175,000.
records.best_fit: International first-year or transfer applicants to Middlebury who can document financial need through the CSS Profile and, for international parents, non-US tax forms or employer earning statements, and who can meet the published financial aid deadline for their application round.
records.eligibility_summary: Aid is awarded to admitted Middlebury undergraduates on demonstrated financial need only; the College publishes '100% Calculated Need Met', '100% Need-Based Aid' and a $66K average grant across all recipients, and states it meets the full demonstrated financial need of admitted undergraduates. Every prospective undergraduate applying for aid must file the CSS Profile (Middlebury College school code 3526), and international students must submit it electronically because the College does not accept the ISFAA or a paper copy; international applicants also submit parent non-US tax forms or employer earning statements translated into English, plus a parent non-filing statement where applicable, through the College Board IDOC service. The FAFSA (school code 003691) is required for US citizens and eligible noncitizens. About 15% of Middlebury students carry international passports or were raised outside the United States. No per-annum amount, currency or period is published for this aid, and no separate merit scholarship for international applicants was confirmed on the official pages read.

records.name: President's International Distinction Scholarship
records.duration: Payable over 4 years, covering the first four years of the undergraduate degree
records.deadline: The deadline for application-based scholarships is January 10. For undergraduate students starting at the U of A in September 2027, the scholarship application will open Oct. 1, 2026 and close Jan. 10, 2027.
records.application_period: Entrance scholarship applications through the U of A Awards Hub run from Oct. 1 to Jan. 10. For students starting in September 2027 the window opens October 1, 2026 and closes January 10, 2027. Offers are made starting in early winter.
records.application_method: Separate application, not automatic on admission. The University of Alberta states: 'You must apply to an undergraduate degree program before you can apply for any entrance scholarships.' Applicants then submit one single scholarship application through the U of A Awards Hub (https://alberta.academicworks.ca/), which assesses them for all application-based awards including this one. Admission-based awards by contrast require no scholarship application and are assessed from the admission average at the time of the admission offer; this award is listed among the application-based awards.
records.description: The President's International Distinction Scholarship is the University of Alberta's most prestigious and competitive scholarship for international students. Each year 25 students with a superior admission average and demonstrated leadership qualities entering their first year of an undergraduate degree on a student visa permit receive up to CAN $120,000, payable over four years. It is an application-based award: applicants must first apply to an undergraduate degree program, then submit the University's single scholarship application, which for September 2027 entry closes January 10, 2027. The University of Alberta states that it does not offer full scholarships for either domestic or international students, so this award does not cover the whole cost of an international degree.
records.best_fit: High-achieving applicants from outside Canada who will enter the first year of a full-time undergraduate degree at the University of Alberta on a student visa permit, have a superior admission average, and can evidence leadership in school, community organisations, extracurricular activities or the workplace. Published winners have entered BEng, BSc, BAEcon, BCom, BA/BSc and BSc (Hons) programmes across Engineering, Science, Arts and Business.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be entering directly from high school, must be entering the first year of full-time studies in an undergraduate degree program at the University of Alberta in September of the upcoming year, must be studying on a student visa permit, must meet or exceed the required admission average (the award page describes this as a 'superior admission average') and must demonstrate leadership qualities. An admission application must be submitted before any entrance scholarship application can be made. Entrance award offers are conditional on the accuracy of self-recorded grades. official_details.description: The President's International Distinction Scholarship is the University of Alberta's most prestigious and competitive scholarship for international students. Each year 25 students with a superior admission average and demonstrated leadership qualities entering their first year of an undergraduate degree on a student visa permit receive up to CAN $120,000, payable over four years. It is an application-based award: applicants must first apply to an undergraduate degree program, then submit the University's single scholarship application by January 10, and offers are made starting in early winter. The University of Alberta states that it does not offer full scholarships for either domestic or international students, so the award funds part rather than all of the cost of an international degree.
official_details.coverage: Cash scholarship of up to CAN $120,000 payable over four years, to 25 recipients per year. Not a full-cost award. The University of Alberta's International Tuition + Fees page identifies the four cost components of an international degree - instructional tuition fees, non-instructional fees, books and supplies, and living arrangement - none of which is separately covered by this award.

records.description: The President's International Entrance Scholarship is the University of Guelph's flagship international entrance award for students entering semester one of any degree program while paying international tuition. Value is banded on the admission average and payable over four years: for the 2027 entry cycle a 95.0%+ admission average receives $20,000 in year 1 plus $7,500 in each of years 2-4, a total of $42,500 CAD. Awarded automatically with the offer of admission, it requires no separate application. It is a partial award, not a tuition waiver: recipients must continue to pay full international tuition and fees, and years 2-4 are conditional on maintaining a minimum 80.0% average while registered full-time.

Selection is banded on the admission average calculated by U of G Admission Services (Canadian curriculum grading scale or equivalent as determined by International Admission). Recipients must register full-time in both the fall and winter semesters, must continue to pay international tuition and fees, and must achieve a minimum 80.0% average in their previous academic year of full-time study to receive years 2-4.

official_details.description: The President's International Entrance Scholarship is the University of Guelph's flagship automatic-on-admission international entrance award. U of G states that international students can 'Earn up to $42,500 CAD in international entrance scholarships over four years!' and that these awards are 'Receive a guaranteed entrance scholarship based on your admission average, payable over four years. No scholarship application is required, with eligible students being notified through their offer of admission.' For the 2027 entry cycle, year 1 is banded from $10,000 (70.0-84.9% admission average) to $20,000 (95.0%+) and years 2-4 pay $7,500 per year, giving four-year totals from $32,500 to $42,500 CAD. The award is limited to international applicants paying international tuition who are entering semester one of any degree program and have not previously attended post-secondary study. It is a partial award: recipients must continue to pay international tuition and fees.
official_details.program_type: University merit scholarship (international entrance, automatic on admission)
official_details.coverage: Tuition-fee credit applied to the University of Guelph student account in two equal payments over the fall and winter semesters, with conditional renewal in years 2-4. No living-cost, travel or health-insurance coverage.

application_readiness_checklist: Apply to the University of Guelph through the international undergraduate admission application and complete every item Admission Services requests.
Send the curriculum-specific supporting documentation for your education system early; the scholarship decision is triggered when Admission Services has received it, not when you apply.

Check your admission average against the published bands (70.0-84.9%, 85.0-89.9%, 90.0-94.9%, 95.0%+) and aim for the top band, since each band step changes both the year 1 amount and the four-year total.
Read the offer of admission carefully: the scholarship is announced with the offer, so there is nothing separate to submit afterwards.
If you miss the band on your first offer, remember the University re-considered in May and August, so keep your marks up in later terms.
Budget for the international difference: the award is applied to your student account as tuition credit but does not remove the requirement to pay international tuition and fees.
If you are transferring rather than entering from high school, check the separate International Transfer Scholarship instead; the transfer route is not covered by this award.
Use the Undergraduate Award Search to see whether additional awards in your program or college stack with this one.
common_rejection_risks: Deferring the offer of admission: entrance scholarships cannot be deferred, and the deferred applicant is only reconsidered the following year based on availability.
Falling below the 80.0% renewal average in a full-time year, which cancels years 2-4; lost payments cannot be added to the end of the award period.
Dropping below full-time registration in either the fall or winter semester, which reduces or cancels the award value.
Paying domestic tuition and fees after the offer, which downgrades the award to the domestic University of Guelph Entrance Scholarship (E0291) values.
Having previous post-secondary study: the award requires that the applicant has not attended a post-secondary institution.
Incomplete supporting documentation, so Admission Services never triggers the scholarship consideration.
Assuming a March 8, 2027 deadline applies here; that date is for the Dr. Franco J. Vaccarino President's Scholarship only, and missing it forfeits that separate $42,500 award.
Planning a major or college change that breaks a related college-specific international Dean's award renewal condition.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Full international tuition remains payable in full: the University publishes $46,780 CAD (most Bachelor of Arts/Science programs) to $66,099 CAD (Bachelor of Computing, Bachelor of Engineering) per year on a 2025-26 basis, and $101,634 CAD for the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine.
Compulsory fees of $1,748-$2,297 CAD per year are not covered.
University Health Insurance Plan (UHIP) of $948 CAD per year is not covered.
Textbooks estimated at $1,400 CAD per year are not covered.
Residence room of $8,387-$11,742 CAD per year is not covered, except for the 2 winners of the separate Vaccarino President's Scholarship who receive guaranteed on-campus residence.
A mandatory meal plan of $5,750-$7,850 CAD per year in residence is not covered.
Personal expenses estimated at $2,500 CAD per year are not covered.
A non-refundable tuition deposit of $2,000 CAD is required to show commitment.
Immigration Canada requires proof of funds for one full year of tuition and living expenses for a study permit, and the University warns about its 'Fees Guarantee' cap of 5% annual tuition increases.
Travel costs are explicitly outside the estimate; the University's own guidance says to factor in travel and equipment fees separately.

Entrants must complete the Pearson entry form, write a short response about why they chose UM and their best PTE preparation tip, and apply to at least one eligible Universiti Malaya programme (Bachelor's, Master's or Doctoral) for the listed intakes. records.name: Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship
records.program_type: University-level undergraduate scholarship (automatic consideration with admission)
records.official_source: National University of Singapore (NUS), Office of Admissions
records.duration: Tenable for the normal candidature period of the undergraduate programme at NUS. NUS publishes no fixed number of years for the award; the duration follows the candidature period of the specific degree programme entered.
records.deadline: No separate scholarship deadline is published. The official Important Dates and Application page lists the application period for this scholarship as "Based on admissions application timeline", with the qualification requirement stated as "High school qualifications eligible for admission to NUS" and the note "All eligible students will be considered for the scholarship through their application for undergraduate admission to NUS." Shortlisting interviews are conducted from January to July and interviewed candidates are informed of the outcome by mid-July.
records.application_period: There is no scholarship application window of its own. Consideration is automatic and runs on the NUS undergraduate admissions timeline for the intake concerned, so the effective window is the admission application period for your qualification. The award page states that "Candidates will be considered and shortlisted for the scholarship through their application for undergraduate admission to NUS" and "All eligible students applying for undergraduate admission to NUS will be considered for this scholarship." NUS states that only shortlisted candidates are informed by e-mail, that selection interviews are conducted from January to July, and that interviewed candidates are informed of the scholarship outcomes by mid-July. The 1 February to 19 March 2027 window published on the same site applies to Scholarships for Freshmen (Singapore Citizens) and is expressly not the window for this international scholarship.
application_method: This is NOT a separate application. The scholarship requires no scholarship form, no scholarship portal submission and no additional deadline.
Submit a single application for undergraduate admission to NUS through the official NUS Applicant Portal, using a high school qualification eligible for admission to NUS.

Choose an eligible first-degree programme in Computing, Engineering (excluding Infrastructure and Project Management) or Science (excluding Environmental Studies and Pharmacy); the scholarship is restricted to the programmes NUS lists in its Terms and Conditions.
Ensure the strength of that admission application is visible, because NUS states that invited applicants are assessed for scholarship suitability based on the strength of their application.
Wait for NUS to contact you: only applicants shortlisted for the selection interview(s) are informed via e-mail.
Attend the selection interview(s) when they are conducted, between January and July.
On award, take up the MOE Tuition Grant and accept the six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation.
records.description: The Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship is a freshmen scholarship offered by NUS to support outstanding Asian students (excluding Singapore citizens) who apply for a full-time undergraduate degree programme in Computing, Engineering (excluding Infrastructure and Project Management) or Science (excluding Environmental Studies and Pharmacy). Candidates are considered and shortlisted automatically through their application for undergraduate admission to NUS, with no separate scholarship application. The award pays 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant, a S$6,000 annual living allowance, an annual accommodation allowance set at the lowest on-campus double room rate, a one-time S$1,750 computer allowance, a one-time S$200 settling-in allowance, and a travel allowance for the incoming and return passage. Recipients must serve a six-year bond with a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation, and the scholarship is renewed every semester provided the scholar maintains a GPA of at least 3.50 (or equivalent) and good conduct.
records.best_fit: Outstanding high-school leavers who are citizens of an Asian country or region other than Singapore, hold outstanding high school results with an excellent co-curricular record and demonstrated leadership, and are applying to a first-year NUS degree programme in Computing, Engineering or Science. It suits applicants who can meet the six-year post-graduation work bond with a Singapore-registered company and who accept that at least 75% of their graduation credits must be earned in Singapore.
records.eligibility_summary: Open to citizens of an Asian country or region, excluding Singapore, who apply for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme in Computing, Engineering (excluding Infrastructure and Project Management) or Science (excluding Environmental Studies and Pharmacy) at NUS. Applicants must have outstanding high school results, an excellent co-curricular activities record, and strong leadership qualities and potential. Transfer applicants from local or overseas universities are not eligible. The scholarship is considered and shortlisted automatically through the applicant's application for undergraduate admission to NUS. It is tenable for the normal candidature period of the programme, renewed every semester provided the scholar maintains a GPA of at least 3.50 (or equivalent) and good conduct, and carries a six-year bond to serve with a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation. Recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant and may not hold any other scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance, and at least 75% of the credits/units required for graduation must be earned in Singapore.

records.notes: Award amounts other than the S$6,000 annual living allowance, which is the single figure used in funding_amount: the S$1,750 one-time computer allowance, the S$200 one-time settling-in allowance, and the accommodation allowance, which NUS states only as an amount equivalent to the lowest double room rate for on-campus accommodation and does not publish as a fixed sum. The travel allowance is likewise not quantified by NUS and is payable only against the incoming and return passage, subject to proof of employment. The six-year bond to serve with a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation is a service obligation, so fully_funded is recorded as false even though tuition is fully covered at the subsidised rate. Tuition coverage is stated only against subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant, so the gap to the full international tuition rate is not covered. NUS publishes no English language requirement, no document checklist specific to this scholarship, and no numerical selection weighting. The award is listed by NUS under both Scholarships for Freshmen (Singapore Permanent Residents) and Scholarships for Freshmen (International Students), while the scholarship page itself frames it as support for outstanding Asian students excluding Singapore citizens; the eligibility criteria reproduced here are the ones stated on the scholarship page. This record is deliberately kept distinct from the NUS International Undergraduate Scholarship already in the database (programme_details id 105), which is open to citizens of all countries except Singapore and carries different allowance amounts (S$5,800 living, S$5,000 accommodation, no settling-in or travel allowance).

records.description: Southern Methodist University in Dallas automatically considers every applicant, regardless of citizenship, for its academic merit scholarships when they apply for admission by 1 November (Early Action / Early Decision I) or 15 January (Regular Decision / Early Decision II). International applicants receive merit aid only: SMU states that need-based financial aid is available only for U.S. citizens or permanent U.S. residents. Individual awards range from a flat USD 7,500 per academic year (International Baccalaureate Scholarship) to about 75 percent of tuition and fees (Nancy Ann and Ray L. Hunt Leadership Scholarship) and full tuition and fees plus a housing scholarship (President's Scholarship). Most awards are stackable but the combined total cannot exceed the cost of tuition and fees.
records.best_fit: International first-year applicants with a very strong academic record who are applying to a selective private research university in the United States and can demonstrate the high-school curriculum rigor, GPA and, unless they score highly on SAT/ACT writing, standardised test results SMU looks for in its merit pool.
records.eligibility_summary: Open to applicants of any nationality: "All students who apply to SMU, regardless of citizenship, are automatically considered for SMU's generous academic merit scholarships." There is no separate scholarship application. Need-based financial aid is explicitly closed to international students ("Need-based financial aid is available only for U.S. citizens or permanent U.S. residents"). Applicants must be first-year, apply by the 1 November or 15 January deadline to be considered, and satisfy the standard undergraduate admission requirements (transcript, essay, required counsellor recommendation, optional teacher recommendation and resume, optional SAT/ACT). English proficiency scores are required only where the high-school language of instruction is bilingual or not solely English. Several awards are restricted to particular curricula (International Baccalaureate Diploma, Dallas County high schools, North Dallas High School) and to U.S. citizens or permanent residents where need-based aid is involved.

SMU notes that applicants who submit no SAT or ACT scores "will be considered only for artistic scholarship and need-based aid; they will not be considered for scholarships based on academic merit," and that the recommended combined score for academic-merit scholarship consideration is 1380 on the SAT (critical reading and math only) or 29 on the ACT. official_details.description: Southern Methodist University in Dallas, Texas automatically considers every applicant, regardless of citizenship, for its academic merit scholarships as part of the undergraduate admission application; SMU states there is no separate application process. International applicants are eligible on the same nationality basis as everyone else, but need-based financial aid is closed to them and is available only to U.S. citizens and permanent U.S. residents. The merit family comprises the President's Scholarship (full tuition and fees, one study abroad experience, and a housing scholarship for on-campus students), the Nancy Ann and Ray L. Hunt Leadership Scholarship (about 75 percent of tuition and fees plus a study abroad experience), the Provost, SMU Distinguished, Second Century and University Scholarships (partial or full tuition), the International Baccalaureate Scholarship (USD 7,500 per academic year), the Dallas County Promise Scholarship, the Mustang Scholarship and the Robert H. Dedman SMU Scholarship. Most awards are stackable but the combined total cannot exceed the cost of tuition and fees, so none of them is a complete cost-of-study package.
official_details.coverage: Merit tuition assistance only, capped at the cost of tuition and fees. Named award values range from USD 7,500 per academic year to full tuition and fees. Room and board is covered only under the President's Scholarship housing scholarship for on-campus students, and only that award plus the Mustang and Dedman awards include housing. Living expenses, travel, visa and I-20 issuance costs, insurance and health costs are not covered by any of these awards.

application_readiness_checklist: File the SMU undergraduate admission application by 1 November 2026 (Early Action / Early Decision I) or 15 January 2027 (Regular Decision / Early Decision II); there is no separate scholarship form to file
Get the required counsellor recommendation in hand before you submit, because it is the one recommendation SMU marks required
Submit SAT or ACT scores if you want to be considered for academic-merit scholarships - SMU states that applicants with no test scores are considered only for artistic scholarship and need-based aid
Aim for the published merit benchmark of SAT 1380 (critical reading and math) or ACT 29 if your test scores are the weaker part of your file
Have TOEFL, IELTS, DET or PTE results ready if your secondary school's language of instruction is bilingual or not solely English, or if you cannot claim the SAT 580+ / ACT 25+ writing waiver
Do not spend money on a CSS Profile or FAFSA - SMU need-based aid is closed to international students and none of the merit awards depends on those forms
Draft the extra President's Scholarship essay, or the Hunt Leadership essay plus a YouTube video statement, well ahead of the 1 November deadline if you are targeting those two awards
Budget for the costs these awards do not touch: on-campus housing, food, books, health insurance, airfare, visa and I-20 issuance fees
Check whether your own high school is inside or outside Dallas County before chasing the Mustang, Dedman or Dallas County Promise awards, which are geography-restricted
common_rejection_risks: Missing the scholarship-consideration deadline - 15 January is the stated priority deadline for merit scholarship consideration, and later applications are considered for admission only if space is available
Submitting no SAT or ACT scores, which removes you from academic-merit scholarship consideration entirely
Not knowing that need-based aid is unavailable to international students and applying for financial aid that does not exist for you
Omitting the additional essay or YouTube video statement for the President's or Hunt Leadership Scholarships and so being considered only for the automatic pool
Treating stackable awards as a guaranteed full package; SMU caps the combined total at tuition and fees
Overlooking that the Mustang, Robert H. Dedman and Dallas County Promise awards are restricted to specific local high schools
Missing English proficiency documentation where the school's language of instruction is not solely English
Failing to secure the required counsellor recommendation

records.description: The Tasmanian Aurora Excellence Scholarship is the University of Tasmania's highest academic-merit international scholarship. It provides eligible commencing international students with a 50% reduction in registered tuition fees for the duration of their course, applied as a tuition fee credit after each census date. Bachelor's and honours coursework programs are eligible apart from a named exclusion list, so the award is funded at undergraduate level as well as postgraduate. Selection uses a minimum 90 ATAR or equivalent, an application form, a 300-500 word personal statement and an interview. The benefit is tuition only: the Terms and Conditions state the scholarship does not apply to the Student Services and Amenity Fee, accommodation, insurance, books or other non-tuition costs, and is not redeemable for cash.
records.best_fit: High-achieving international applicants with a 90 ATAR or equivalent (or a UTAS degree-level GPA of 6.5/7) who are seeking the largest tuition discount UTAS offers to international students. Because the application is invitation-triggered and runs off the Tasmanian International Merit Scholarship offer route, it suits applicants strong enough on merit to be issued that offer.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be classified as an International Student under the University of Tasmania's Application rules, meet the minimum academic requirements (90 ATAR or equivalent; 6.5/7 GPA where the highest qualification is UTAS degree-level study), be enrolled full-time in an eligible undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree, not be a student from a Transnational Education (TNE) partner affiliated with the University, not be in receipt of any other University of Tasmania scholarship or any external sponsorship, not be commencing through an articulation agreement with a partner institution, and be commencing the first year of their program from 2027. The Terms and Conditions add that applicants must commence study for the first time, must not have previously commenced a course at the University, must hold a valid offer, must meet admission and English language requirements, and must remain eligible for an Australian student visa where applicable. Named excluded undergraduate programs are the Bachelor of Medical Science and Doctor of Medicine, the Bachelor of Nursing in the Hobart campus, the Bachelor of Applied Science (Nautical Science) and (Marine Engineering), and the Advanced Diploma of Applied Science (Nautical Science) and (Marine Engineering). The scholarship is also not available for fully online programs, foundation studies, non-award study, micro credentials, single unit study, exchange programs, government sponsored students, study through the International Pathway College, or study undertaken at a university location outside Australia unless the University approves in writing.

records.selection_notes: Applications are assessed on three published components: meeting the minimum academic requirements for the highest-level qualification (secondary, diploma and degree level of a minimum one-year duration), completion of the application form, and a Personal Statement of 300-500 words. Shortlisted applicants are contacted for an interview after the deadline has closed, so interview performance is the final stage. Applications are assessed for all semester intakes and selection is based on the applicant's highest-level qualification of a minimum of one-year's duration or equivalent. The Terms and Conditions state that scholarships are awarded based on satisfaction of eligibility requirements, published selection criteria which may include academic merit, and available scholarship funding, and that the University may establish scholarship quotas, market-specific allocations or strategic recruitment priorities. All University decisions are final and not subject to review. No published weighting between the assessment components and no published number of awards.
records.notes: NAME MISMATCH WITH THE ASSIGNMENT ROW. Row b115 assigned "International Excellence Scholarship - University of Tasmania". The University of Tasmania publishes no award under that name. official_details.tuition_coverage_note: The award is a partial tuition waiver, not a full one. The Terms and Conditions state it "provides a tuition fee scholarship equivalent to 50% of the published international tuition fees charged for the enrolled units in each study period for the standard duration of the eligible course, up to a maximum of five years full-time equivalent study", and the page's Value field reads "50% reduction in registered tuition fees for the duration of the course." It covers tuition fees only, at 50%, and the same clause states it "applies only to tuition fees" and "does not apply to Student Services and Amenity Fee (SSAF), accommodation, insurance, books or other non-tuition costs". It also "does not apply beyond the standard published duration of an eligible course", "does not apply to repeated units" and "does not apply to units undertaken in excess of course requirements unless approved in writing by the University". Because half of tuition and every non-tuition cost remain payable by the student, fully_funded is false. No absolute dollar figure is published, so funding_amount and funding_currency are null.

records.name: University of Ljubljana Tuition Fee Exemption for International Students
records.duration: No fixed award term is published. The exemption holds for the duration of the student's full-time study for as long as the exemption conditions continue to be met, and is carried forward through enrolment each academic year rather than granted for a set number of years.
records.deadline: No application deadline is published. The University states the exemption for "full-time bachelor's and master's studies" as a standing rule and publishes no application window, no closing date and no separate scholarship call for it.
records.application_period: No application period. There is no application window to open or close: the exemption is a standing tuition rule applied in the ordinary course of enrolment into full-time study, and the University publishes only a current price list, republished each academic year.
records.application_method: Automatic on enrolment — there is no separate application. The University publishes who is exempt from paying tuition fees and who is obliged to pay; the exemption is settled through the enrolment process at the University of Ljubljana member institution (faculty or academy) in which the student enrols, and no scholarship application form or selection round exists for it.
records.description: The University of Ljubljana publishes a standing tuition-fee exemption rather than an open international scholarship competition. Full-time bachelor's and master's study is fee-free for Slovenians (including Slovenians abroad and persons without Slovenian citizenship as defined by Slovenian law), citizens of EU countries plus Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, nationals of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia under bilateral education agreements with the Republic of Slovenia, permanent residents of the Republic of Slovenia who are taxpayers, persons granted international protection or under temporary protection, holders of Republic of Slovenia scholarships (CMEPIUS, JŠRIPSRS) and exchange students. Citizens of non-EU countries with which Slovenia has no bilateral agreement are explicitly listed as obliged to pay, as are all part-time students. The exemption removes the tuition fee only; enrolment fees and study contributions, compulsory health insurance, accommodation and living costs are not covered. The University also publishes two schemes of its own for international students, the Residency of Prof. Grega Košak and the Heart UL campaign, neither of which is a tuition scholarship.
records.best_fit: Full-time applicants who already hold a nationality or residence status that the University lists as fee-exempt, chiefly nationals of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia, EU/EEA-plus citizens studying in Slovenia, permanent residents of Slovenia who are tax residents, and holders of international or temporary protection. Not suitable as a funding route for a full-fee-paying non-EEA applicant, and not suitable for part-time study, which the University lists among those who must pay.
records.eligibility_summary: Eligibility is decided by nationality, residence status and study mode, not by academic merit or competition. The University states that no tuition fees are payable for full-time bachelor's and master's studies by Slovenians (including those living outside Slovenia and those without Slovenian citizenship as defined by the relevant law), students from EU countries together with Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, students from countries with which the Republic of Slovenia has concluded a bilateral agreement (Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia), students with permanent residence in the Republic of Slovenia who themselves or their parents/guardians are taxpayers of the Republic of Slovenia, persons granted international protection and persons under temporary protection, scholarship holders of the Republic of Slovenia (CMEPIUS, Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia), and exchange students including doctoral exchange students. The University states that tuition fees are paid by citizens of non-EU countries with which the Republic of Slovenia has not signed a bilateral agreement, by all students with an already acquired equivalent degree, by exempt students who change study programme or direction and enrol in the same or a lower study year after having exercised the right to repeat a year, by exempt students who re-enrol in the same study programme or direction from which they previously withdrew, by all part-time students, and by all doctoral students. No field or faculty restriction applies to the exemption, although the fee amount itself is published per member institution.

records.notes: SCOPE CORRECTION, stated plainly because the assigned award name was wrong. The b46 assignment row names a 'Jasminka Scholarship - University of Ljubljana'. No award of that name exists on the University of Ljubljana site. The University's own English scholarships page (https://www.uni-lj.si/en/study/scholarships, fetched 2026-10-03) lists only two University-run schemes for international students, the Residency of Prof. Grega Košak (a 4.5-month artist/designer/restorer residency, not a degree scholarship) and the Heart UL campaign (fundraising for enrolled students in financial emergency, not a tuition scholarship), and it refers all state scholarships for international students to the Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia at srips-rs.si. 'Jasminka' is most plausibly a machine-generated garbling of the Fund's Slovenian name, Javni stipendijski, razvojni, invalidski in prezivninski sklad Republike Slovenije; that Fund is a different awarding body, so recording its Zois scholarships or its nationality-locked open calls (Western Balkans, Senegal/Nepal/East Timor, Angola, Ethiopia/Uganda/Rwanda, Türkiye refugees, Palestinian nationals) as a University of Ljubljana award would be a provenance error, and several of those calls are master's-only or locked to nationalities in excluded regions. This record therefore covers the only broad bachelor's-level funding instrument the University itself publishes: the statutory tuition-fee exemption for international students. It is a TUITION REDUCTION, not a scholarship: it is automatic on enrolment, has no application, no deadline, no competition, no stipend and no cash amount, and it applies only to the tuition fee. funding_amount is null on purpose: the University publishes the 2026/2027 tuition and study-contribution amounts as one PDF price list per faculty/academy plus separate lists for enrolment fees and study contributions, doctoral study and interdisciplinary bachelor programmes, and those PDFs were not opened for this record, so no EUR figure is recorded rather than inventing one. Those per-faculty tables mean the fee waived is field-specific in value, but the exemption itself is not restricted by field or faculty. No bond, service obligation or repayment clause is published; the exemption is a fee rule, and the conditions that can withdraw it (changing programme and enrolling in the same or a lower year after a repeat year, or re-enrolling in a programme previously withdrawn from) are recorded as award_holder_conditions. The same exemption rule covers full-time master's study; only the bachelor's level is recorded in degree_levels, and the doctoral level is explicitly excluded because the University lists all doctoral students as obliged to pay. Two official pages and the logo asset were fetched in total; no page was unreachable, but the per-faculty price-list PDFs, the Call for Enrolment for non-EU nationals, the international-students cost-of-living page and the Heart UL FAQ were not fetched, so amounts, enrolment deadlines and English-language requirements are recorded as null rather than guessed.

official_details.application_cycle: Not an application cycle. The exemption is a standing rule for full-time study, and the University republishes the exemption conditions and the tuition and study-contribution price lists each academic year; the price lists on the page are for academic year 2026/2027.
official_details.deadline_central_display: No application deadline is published. The University states the exemption applies to "full-time bachelor's and master's studies" and publishes no opening date, closing date or call for applications for it.
official_details.deadline_note: There is no application window to record, so deadline_central, deadline_central_timezone and deadline_institutional are all null. The exemption is not applied for on a deadline; it is settled when the student enrols in full-time study, and the University publishes the rule rather than a call. Enrolment deadlines for foreign nationals from non-EU member states exist as a separate published Call for Enrolment, but that call governs admission, not this exemption, and it was not fetched, so no date and no timezone are claimed. Any such University of Ljubljana deadline would fall in Europe/Ljubljana time, but no published time was read, so the field stays null.
official_details.status_note: Continuously in force for full-time study; the University published the current conditions and the 2026/2027 price lists at the time of verification on 2026-10-03. There is no open or closed window because there is no application. The exemption is periodically revised by statute and the fee amounts are reissued every academic year, so the status refers to the standing rule, not to a cycle that can close.
official_details.funding_duration: For the duration of the student's full-time study for as long as the exemption conditions are met, carried forward through enrolment each academic year; the University publishes no fixed award term.
official_details.tuition_coverage_note: Covers the tuition fee in full for full-time bachelor's and master's study, and nothing else. It does not cover enrolment fees and study contributions, compulsory health insurance, accommodation, living costs, study materials or travel, and it carries no cash payment. The University lists all part-time students among those obliged to pay tuition fees, so the exemption is void for part-time enrolment. It is also lost by exempt students who change study programme or direction and enrol in the same or a lower study year after already having exercised the right to repeat a year, and by exempt students who re-enrol in the same study programme or direction from which they previously withdrew, as both groups are expressly listed as obliged to pay. Because the award is tuition-only and leaves the remaining components of the cost of study payable, fully_funded is false.
official_details.funding_label: Full tuition fee waived for full-time study; enrolment fees and study contributions, health insurance, accommodation and living costs all remain payable by the student. No stipend, no cash amount, no bond or service obligation.
