official_details.citizenship_residency: Determined by nationality, residence status and protection status rather than by merit. The University lists Slovenians (including those abroad and those without Slovenian citizenship as defined by the relevant law), citizens of EU countries plus Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, nationals of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia under bilateral education agreements, permanent residents of the Republic of Slovenia who are taxpayers of the Republic of Slovenia, persons granted international protection and persons under temporary protection, Republic of Slovenia scholarship holders and exchange students. Citizens of non-EU countries with which the Republic of Slovenia has not signed a bilateral agreement are expressly listed as obliged to pay.
official_details.international_eligibility: For the group this record is aimed at, the University publishes no open international scholarship competition: the only international schemes it runs are the Residency of Prof. Grega Košak, a 4.5-month residency for artists, designers, restorers, theorists and researchers from around the world, and the Heart UL campaign for enrolled students in financial emergency, neither of which funds a bachelor's degree's tuition. Non-EEA nationals of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia qualify for the tuition exemption through a bilateral education agreement with the Republic of Slovenia, and persons granted international protection or under temporary protection qualify irrespective of nationality; all other non-EEA nationals are listed as paying. Scholarships linked from the University's page for international students, such as the Zois scholarships and the various open calls, are awarded by the Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia and are not University of Ljubljana awards.
official_details.study_mode: Full-time only; the University lists all part-time students among those obliged to pay tuition fees.
official_details.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field, subject or faculty restriction on the exemption itself. The amount is field-specific: the University publishes one 2026/2027 price list per member institution (Academy of Fine Arts and Design, Academy of Music, Academy of Theatre Radio Film and Television, Biotechnical Faculty, Faculty of Architecture, Arts, Chemistry and Chemical Technology, Civil and Geodetic Engineering, Computer and Information Science, Education, Electrical Engineering, Health Sciences, Law, Maritime Studies and Transport, Mathematics and Physics, Mechanical Engineering, Medicine, Natural Sciences and Engineering, Pharmacy, Public Administration, Social Sciences, Social Work, Sport, Theology, School of Economics and Business and Veterinary Faculty), plus a separate price list for enrolment fees and study contributions, a separate list for interdisciplinary bachelor degree programmes, a separate list for interdisciplinary and joint master's programmes, a separate doctoral tuition list and a separate set of general conditions for the payment of tuition fees. Doctoral study is explicitly outside the exemption.
official_details.application_method: Automatic on enrolment. The University publishes the exemption as a standing fee rule, so there is no separate application, no application form, no call and no selection process; the exemption is applied in the ordinary course of enrolment.
official_details.application_route: No separate application route. The exemption is applied for in the course of enrolling in full-time study at the University of Ljubljana member institution in which the student studies, under the rules published on the University tuition fees page; the University's Higher Education Application and Information Service handles enrolment.

official_details.english_requirement_note: Neither the University tuition fees page nor the University scholarships page publishes an English-language requirement, test, band or score for this exemption, so the field is null rather than estimated. Language and qualification requirements are set per study programme by the member institution, and the University is a Slovenian-language institution; no IELTS or other figure was read on an official page for this record.
selection_criteria: No selection criteria. The exemption is a standing tuition-fee rule applied by nationality, residence status, protection status, prior degree and study mode, not a competitive award, and the University publishes no shortlist, ranking or interview.
official_details.duration: Duration of the student's full-time study, for as long as the exemption conditions are met; the University publishes no fixed award term for the exemption.
award_holder_conditions: Study must remain full-time for the whole period of the exemption
Exemption is lost on changing study programme or direction and enrolling in the same or a lower study year after having already exercised the right to repeat a year at the same cycle of study
Exemption is lost on re-enrolling in the same study programme or direction from which the student previously withdrew
Enrolment fees and study contributions remain payable and are not covered
No bond, service obligation, work requirement or repayment clause is published for the exemption
supplements_or_initiatives: Heart UL: a University of Ljubljana campaign whose stated aim is to raise funds for students who, due to special personal circumstances, find themselves in a financial emergency and consequently have no means of survival. It is a social-assistance campaign for enrolled students, not a tuition scholarship, and the University publishes no amount for it on the scholarships page.

Residency of Prof. Grega Košak: a University of Ljubljana residency of four and a half months in an apartment in the centre of Ljubljana for artists, designers, restorers, theorists and researchers from around the world. It is a residency, not a degree scholarship, and does not fund a bachelor's programme.

State scholarships for international students listed on the University page, including Zois scholarships and various open calls, are administered and awarded by the Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia (srips-rs.si), not by the University; the University states that the Fund publishes the open call defining all requirements, procedures and the amount of scholarship grants.
Republic of Slovenia scholarship holders, including CMEPIUS holders, are listed by the University as exempt from tuition fees, so a state scholarship can also remove the tuition fee for the holder.

official_details.description: A statutory tuition-fee exemption applied by the University of Ljubljana, not a competitive scholarship. Full-time bachelor's and master's study is fee-free for Slovenians (including Slovenians abroad and persons without Slovenian citizenship as defined by the relevant law), citizens of EU countries plus Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, nationals of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia under bilateral education agreements, permanent residents of the Republic of Slovenia who are taxpayers, persons granted international protection or under temporary protection, Republic of Slovenia scholarship holders and exchange students. Citizens of non-EU countries with which the Republic of Slovenia has not signed a bilateral agreement, all part-time students, all doctoral students and all students holding an equivalent degree are obliged to pay. There is no application, no deadline, no competition, no stipend and no bond, and only the tuition fee is removed: enrolment fees and study contributions, health insurance, accommodation and living costs stay payable, so the award is not fully funded.
official_details.coverage: Tuition fee only, for full-time study, until the exemption conditions cease to apply. Enrolment fees and study contributions, compulsory health insurance, accommodation, living costs, study materials and travel are all outside the coverage.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality or residence status appears in the University's fee-exempt list before you rely on this: EU plus Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway; Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia; permanent residence in Slovenia with tax residency; or international or temporary protection.
If you are a citizen of a non-EU country with no bilateral agreement with Slovenia, stop here: the University lists you among those obliged to pay, and this exemption is not available to you.
Enrol in full-time study only. Part-time enrolment puts you in the group the University lists as obliged to pay, and the exemption will not be applied.
Check you do not already hold an equivalent degree of education, which also puts you in the paying group.
Budget separately for everything the exemption does not touch: enrolment fee and study contributions, compulsory health insurance, accommodation and living costs, study materials and travel.
Open the price list for your own faculty or academy for the relevant academic year, rather than assuming the fee is the same across the University, and use that figure in your funding plan.

If you are changing study programme or direction, or re-enrolling in a programme you previously left, raise it with the enrolling faculty before enrolling, because both situations are listed as forfeiting the exemption.
Contact the University or the enrolling member institution in writing to have your exemption status confirmed for your specific nationality and residence combination before you commit funds.
If you already hold a Republic of Slovenia scholarship such as CMEPIUS or a JŠRIPSRS award, tell the enrolling institution, as scholarship holders are listed as fee-exempt.

Consider the Fund's separate state scholarship routes for non-EEA nationals, but note those are awarded by the Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia and are outside this record
common_rejection_risks: Assuming this is an open scholarship anyone can apply for. It is a standing fee rule, so there is no application to submit and no outcome to be rejected from; if your nationality is not on the exempt list, the fee simply applies.
Enrolling part-time and losing the exemption without realising it, because the University lists all part-time students as obliged to pay.
Already holding an equivalent degree and therefore being liable for the full fee.
Changing study programme or direction and enrolling in the same or a lower study year after having repeated a year, which the University lists as forfeiting the exemption.
Re-enrolling in the same study programme or direction previously withdrawn from, which the University also lists as forfeiting the exemption.
Assuming the Western Balkans agreement extends to all non-EEA countries. The University names Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo and Serbia only.
Treating the exemption as fully funding the degree and being caught short on living costs in Ljubljana, which the fee waiver does nothing about.
Reading a third-party listing that calls this a 'Jasminka Scholarship'. No award of that name appears on the University of Ljubljana site.
Missing the annual change of fee tables and planning a budget from a previous academic year's per-faculty amount.
Assuming a state scholarship amount applies here. The Zois scholarships and the Fund's open calls named on the University page are awarded by the Fund, not the University.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs are the main gap. The exemption waives the tuition fee only and provides no stipend, so the full cost of living in Ljubljana, one of the more expensive capitals in the region, has to be met from other funds. No monthly figure is recorded in this record because the University's own cost-of-living guidance was not fetched; read the University international-students cost-of-living and accommodation pages, or your national scholarship body's published cost-of-living figure for Ljubljana, before budgeting.

Student dormitory rent or private rental, not covered. If you are not a Republic of Slovenia scholarship holder you do not have the subsidised scholarship-holder dormitory route described by the University, so expect the full foreign-student dormitory rate or market rent.
Compulsory health insurance for non-EU nationals, not covered by the fee exemption. Arrange it before the start of studies.

Enrolment fee and study contributions, charged separately from tuition and not covered, even where tuition is waived. Amounts are in the annual price list for enrolment fees and study contributions, which was not opened for this record.

Study materials, equipment and laboratory or fieldwork costs, depending on the faculty. The University's Heart UL campaign exists because enrolled students can face this kind of shortfall, which is why it is not safe to treat the fee waiver as complete funding.
Residence permit and visa costs, and health insurance required for the permit, for non-EU nationals.
Travel to and from Slovenia, which the exemption does not cover in either direction.

The tuition fee itself, for anyone outside the exempt categories, set per faculty and per study programme in the annual price lists. Those PDFs were not opened for this record, so no EUR figure is given here; use the figure for your own faculty.
Lost earnings or opportunity cost, which no fee exemption addresses and which applicants from outside the EEA should treat as a real component of the total cost.
document_audit: The University publishes no document checklist for this exemption, because there is no application. This list is derived guidance, not an official requirement.
Passport or other evidence of nationality, so the enrolling institution can check the fee-exempt nationality list, including the specific countries named under the bilateral agreements.

If you are a national of Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Kosovo or Serbia, the evidence relied on is the bilateral education agreement with the Republic of Slovenia, so confirm with the enrolling institution that it accepts your nationality at face value for fee purposes.
Evidence of permanent residence in the Republic of Slovenia together with tax residency, for you or for your parents or guardians, if you are claiming exemption on that ground.
Evidence of international protection or of temporary protection, if you are claiming exemption on that ground.
Evidence of a Republic of Slovenia scholarship such as CMEPIUS or a JŠRIPSRS award, if you are claiming exemption as a scholarship holder.
Evidence of exchange status, if you are claiming exemption as an exchange student.
Confirm you have no previously awarded equivalent degree, which the University treats as a disqualifying condition for the exemption.
Keep your enrolment confirmation showing full-time status, since the exemption depends on it and is easiest to verify when the faculty can see it at enrolment.
Keep the fee assessment or invoice from your faculty showing the tuition line at zero, so a later change of programme or re-enrolment can be checked against what you were actually charged.

alerts.message: If you are a citizen of a non-EU country with which Slovenia has no bilateral agreement, the University lists you as obliged to pay tuition fees and this exemption does not apply to you. Do not build a funding plan on it.
All part-time students are listed as obliged to pay tuition fees. Only full-time enrolment qualifies for the exemption, so switching to part-time mid-programme can create an immediate fee liability.

Changing programme or direction and enrolling in the same or a lower study year after repeating a year, or re-enrolling in a programme you withdrew from, are both listed as forfeiting the exemption. Clear this with the faculty before enrolling.

The University republishes tuition and study-contribution price lists each academic year, with a separate list per faculty. Never plan from a previous year's figure, and always use the list for your own faculty and programme.

This is a tuition reduction applied automatically on enrolment. There is no application window, no deadline, no shortlist and no award letter to wait for, and there is no application to submit before you enrol.

No 'Jasminka Scholarship' exists at the University of Ljubljana. The University's scholarships page names only the Residency of Prof. Grega Košak, the Heart UL campaign and state scholarships awarded by the Fund at srips-rs.si.

The Zois scholarships and the open calls for foreign nationals linked from the University page are awarded by the Public Scholarship, Development, Disability and Maintenance Fund of the Republic of Slovenia. Check that Fund's own call for deadlines and amounts; they are not covered by this record and are frequently restricted by nationality or to master's level.

submission_workflow: No application exists for this exemption, so there is nothing to submit and no submission deadline to track.

Apply and enrol in full-time study through the ordinary University of Ljubljana admission and enrolment route for your nationality, which for non-EU nationals runs through the published Call for Enrolment and is handled by the Higher Education Application and Information Service at vpis@uni-lj.si.
At enrolment, present the evidence for your fee-exempt nationality, residence or protection status to the enrolling member institution so that the tuition line is assessed at zero.
Check the tuition and study-contribution invoice issued at enrolment and confirm the tuition line is zero and that the remaining enrolment fee and study contributions are as you budgeted.
If the tuition line is not zero, take it up with the enrolling faculty immediately with your exemption evidence, since the exemption is applied at that point rather than awarded later.
Re-confirm full-time status and exemption eligibility at each annual re-enrolment, because the exemption is carried forward through enrolment and is lost if the study mode or the programme changes.
Arrange compulsory health insurance before the start of studies, and separately arrange a residence permit, as neither is included in the fee exemption.
Apply for dormitory accommodation early through the University or the student dormitory, and budget the foreign-student rate if you are not a Republic of Slovenia scholarship holder.

records.description: The Vice Chancellor's International Scholarship is a competitive Griffith University award that reduces tuition fees by 50% for international students commencing undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree programs. It is open to citizens of any country other than Australia or New Zealand who hold an offer of study, need a minimum GPA of 6.0 on a 7-point scale in previous study, and enrol full-time. The 50% reduction is applied before the census date of each trimester for the duration of the degree, on condition that a cumulative GPA of 5.5 on a 7-point scale is maintained. The award covers tuition fees only; the remaining balance, living costs, accommodation and travel are not funded, and no bond or service obligation is attached.
records.best_fit: International students with a strong academic record who already hold, or will receive in time, a Letter of Offer from Griffith for a 2026 or 2027 undergraduate or postgraduate coursework commencement, and who can maintain a cumulative GPA of 5.5 or above on a 7.0 scale.
records.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be a citizen of a country other than Australia or New Zealand, be a new commencing student holding an offer to study issued by the scholarship closing date for their commencing trimester, hold a minimum GPA of 6.0 or above on a 7-point scale (or equivalent) in previous studies, satisfy all academic and English language entry requirements for the chosen undergraduate or postgraduate coursework program, and be a full-time student starting in 2026 or 2027. Applicants must remain International Fee Paying; any change from that status ends the scholarship. The award excludes Higher Degree Research, online (campus = online), non-award, Study Abroad, Diploma, Masters Qualifying, MBA (program code 5158), Griffith English Language Institute programs, part-time-only programs, and programs delivered onshore or offshore in collaboration with a partner organisation.

records.description: Western University's Office of the Registrar offers an unlimited number of Welcome to Canada Admission Scholarships to international students entering full-time first-year study at its main campus. Each award is worth $10,000 for the first year and includes a guaranteed place in on-campus residence for the first two years of study. Consideration is automatic on admission and no application is submitted. The award may not be combined with any other admission scholarship, although the New to Canada Grant is payable on top of it.

Reducing enrolment to part-time or withdrawing from the academic year forfeits eligibility, and any change in Canadian status that qualifies the student for domestic fees after an offer renders them ineligible.

records.notes: Chosen from several distinct international awards on the uwo.ca host. Western publishes an international entrance scholarship pool, three $100,000 International President's Entrance Scholarships, an $80,000 Neen Hodgins President's International Entrance Scholarship, and this Welcome to Canada Admission Scholarship. The Welcome to Canada Admission Scholarship was selected because it is the only one with its own dedicated official award page stating a precise, current benefit (CAD 10,000 first year plus a two-year residence guarantee), an explicit international-only eligibility rule, unlimited availability, and an explicit automatic-on-admission method - i.e. the best-documented award, not the highest-value one. No two records were produced for this host. Separately, the Automatic Admission Scholarships page publishes renewal conditions only for a former 'Western International Admission Scholarship' 'prior to the 2024-2025 academic year', indicating that named award was retired or renamed; no such award is claimed here. No renewal provision is published for the Welcome to Canada Admission Scholarship, which is stated as a first-year amount. This is a partial award: Western publishes an estimated year 1 international tuition and fees range of $48,000 to $64,400, so the $10,000 does not cover tuition. The University also publishes an international Tuition Fee Guarantee capping year-2-onward undergraduate international tuition increases at 4% per year.

TOEFL iBT taken on or after 21 January 2026 (1-6 scale): minimum overall 4.5, minimum 4.0 in reading, speaking and writing, minimum 4.5 in listening. PTE Academic: minimum overall 58, minimum 56 in each section. Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency: minimum overall 176, minimum 169 in each section. CAEL: minimum overall 60, minimum 60 in each section. Duolingo English Test: minimum 115 overall, minimum 100 in each subscore.
official_details.english_requirement_note: These scores are the University admission requirement that an award holder must already have satisfied in order to be admitted, not a condition of the scholarship itself. Western states the tests must be written before March 2027 for fall 2027 admission and that scores from tests written before 1 January 2025 are not accepted. Scores must be sent electronically; IELTS requires the name and date of birth to match the OUAC application, TOEFL uses Western institution code 0984, and paper Test Report Forms are not accepted. Applicants who studied four years of secondary school, two years of Ontario college, or one year of university full-time in English may request an exemption or waiver, which is not granted automatically. Nursing applicants are told their English language requirements are different.

official_details.description: The Welcome to Canada Admission Scholarship is offered by Western University's Office of the Registrar as an unlimited number of awards for international students entering full-time first-year studies at Western's main campus. Each award provides CAD 10,000 for the first year and a guaranteed place in on-campus residence for the first two years of study. Consideration is automatic with the admission application and there is no separate application, no published academic-average threshold and no published selection weighting. The award cannot be combined with any other admission scholarship, although the New to Canada Grant is payable on top of it. It is not a tuition waiver: Western publishes an estimated year 1 international tuition and fees range of CAD 48,000 to 64,400.
official_details.coverage: Covers CAD 10,000 of first-year costs and guarantees on-campus residence for the first two years. It is not a tuition waiver, does not cover the balance of international tuition and fees, and cannot be combined with another admission scholarship.

application_readiness_checklist: Apply to Western through the OUAC portal for first-year study at the main campus, and make sure all supporting documentation is submitted, not just the application form
Confirm your study-permit and funding plan covers international fee-paying status, since any later switch to domestic fee status voids the award
Budget on the basis of international fees: Western estimates year 1 international tuition and fees at CAD 48,000 to CAD 64,400, so CAD 10,000 closes only a fraction of the gap
Sit an accepted English proficiency test early enough that the electronic score reaches Western before the University's stated March 2027 cut-off for fall 2027 entry
Match the first name, surname and date of birth on your test registration exactly to your OUAC application, or Western cannot match the score
Plan for the award to be visible on choose.uwo.ca by the end of April, and check the portal there rather than waiting for a separate email
Decide your residence plans knowing the award guarantees an on-campus place for the first two years
Do not count on stacking this with another Western admission scholarship; the two are mutually exclusive
common_rejection_risks: Completing high school inside Canada, which makes the applicant ineligible for this international-only award
Switching to domestic fee-paying status after the offer, which renders the applicant ineligible
Dropping below 3.5 courses or withdrawing from the academic year, which forfeits the award
Deferring admission, which the University states is not permitted for this award
Applying for another Western admission scholarship as well, since the awards cannot be combined
Sending an English test score that does not match the OUAC personal details, so Western cannot match it
Applying to a part-time or non-first-entry programme rather than a first-entry undergraduate programme of at least 3.5 courses
Assuming the award renews. The published benefit is stated for the first year and no renewal provision is published
estimated_uncovered_costs: International tuition and fees: Western's published estimate is CAD 48,000 to CAD 64,400 for year 1. The award contributes CAD 10,000, leaving roughly CAD 38,000 to CAD 54,400 of tuition and fees to fund yourself
The award is explicitly not a tuition waiver and cannot be combined with another admission scholarship, so this gap cannot be closed by stacking a second Western admission award
Living costs: Western's own estimate of total first-academic-year living costs is CAD 21,770 to CAD 27,340 living in residence, or CAD 14,580 to CAD 31,960 living off campus
The residence guarantee secures a place, not a free place: the residence and meal plan is estimated at CAD 16,510 to CAD 19,140 for eight months and remains payable
Budget for the first year of study only. The published cash figure is for the first year and no renewal provision is published, so later years must be funded separately
Visa, study permit and travel costs: Western advises international students to add these on top of the published cost tables

Allow for rising costs after year 1. Western's international Tuition Fee Guarantee limits undergraduate international tuition increases to 4% per year after Year 1, and student fees and living costs can still rise more
Nursing applicants face different English requirements, which can add an English Boost Program year of cost before the degree begins

alerts.trigger: Mutual exclusivity with other admission scholarships
alerts.message: The Welcome to Canada Admission Scholarship cannot be combined with any other admission scholarship. If you also hold or expect an offer of a Western Scholarship of Excellence, Western Scholarship of Distinction, Western Admission Scholarship, National Scholarship, Schulich Leader Scholarship, Continue in Canada Admission Scholarship or a Faculty of Arts & Humanities Entrance Scholarship, check which one Western will apply, because your fee account can only carry one.

The award is published as '$10,000 for first year' and Western publishes no renewal condition for it. Treat years two onward as unfunded unless the University states otherwise in writing for your entry year.
Do not wait for a scholarship deadline and do not submit a separate scholarship application. There is none. Check choose.uwo.ca by the end of April for the outcome.

For fall 2027 admission Western will not accept English tests written before 1 January 2025, and the test must be written before March 2027. A stale score can invalidate an otherwise complete application.

If anything changes your Canadian immigration status in a way that qualifies you for domestic tuition fees after the offer, Western states you become ineligible for this scholarship. Re-check after any permanent-residency application.

submission_workflow: Choose your Western programme and submit the undergraduate application through the Ontario Universities' Application Centre (OUAC), as international admissions at Western run through OUAC
Upload all supporting documentation to Western; the University requires the complete file, not only the application form

If English is not your first language, book IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency, CAEL or the Duolingo English Test early enough for the electronic result to arrive before the University's March cut-off for the entry year
Use the exact same first name, surname and date of birth on the test registration as on the OUAC application so Western can match the score

Watch for the To Do List item on your Western Student Center account; Western states proof of English proficiency may be requested there, and takes up to two weeks to update the item to 'Received' after a score arrives

If you believe you qualify for an English exemption or waiver, email welcome@uwo.ca with the subject 'English Proficiency Waiver Request' including your OUAC reference number or Western Student Number, and expect to complete an online form and upload transcripts and a school or teacher letter
After admission, monitor choose.uwo.ca from the end of April for the scholarship decision, then accept your offer of admission by the admission response deadline
Register full-time in first-year studies with at least 3.5 courses and pay international student tuition and fees, which is the condition for keeping the award
Note that admission scholarships cannot be deducted from the first installment of fees; Western applies them to the fee account once confirmed, typically before the end of September
